On the Material Cause of Meteors. 23

Its potential existence in the *hyle* <term>Hyle: A Greek term used by ancient and Renaissance philosophers to describe "prime matter," the formless "stuff" of the universe before God gave it shape.</term> or the dark chaos was naturally a companion of potential coldness; this potential then later flowed out with the water in actuality from the darkness at the creation of the world. Therefore, the air has a greater inclination toward a certain occult humidity. This humidity, however, is not part of the essential existence of air, for the air can be converted into an extremely dry nature or condition, as is seen during the summer season. We conclude, therefore, that air is fit to receive any of the four aforementioned qualities <note>The four qualities are Hot, Cold, Moist, and Dry.</note>. It is accustomed to bring this aptitude into action continuously according to the nature and condition of the wind that happens to blow. For example: Northern winds [Aquilonares] make the air cold and dry; Southern winds [Australes] make it hot and moist; the Eastern and the East-Southeast [Eurus] winds make it hot and dry; and Western winds [Occidentales] make it cold and moist. From this, it happens that the quality of the air can be changed at every moment, according to the ordination of GOD, who disposes it according to His will. Indeed, the air receives whatever is infused into it, and yet it nevertheless retains and preserves its spiritual and uniform essence.

CHAPTER V.

*Where the active reason for the air changing from one quality into another is explained. Here it is also taught how it is accustomed to be altered and changed daily from a thin to a thick and visible constitution.*

Although the air (as has already been said) is unique and simple in its nature and existence, nevertheless, through the mediation of the Word and the angelic ministers blowing and moving it with various winds, it is accustomed to migrate from one quality to another. Consequently, it moves from a dense substance into a thin or middling one, and conversely from thin to dense—and this happens daily. For who, experienced in common observation, does not see clouds formed out of the air? And who does not see the very substance of the air condensed into hail, ice, and frost by the northern cold? Holy Scripture teaches us that this cold flows from the divine breath. For (as Job says in chapter 37:9–10), "The mighty GOD brings forth ice by His breath; by the blowing of GOD the frost grows." <note>Original Latin: "Glaciem DEVS fortis edit flatu suo, flante DEO crescit gelu."</note> And elsewhere it is said: "He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs very swiftly. He gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes. He casts forth his ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold?" (Psalm 147:15–17). From this it is clear that thin and invisible air congeals into dense and hard matter through the mediation of the Word of GOD emitting His cold; this Word (as the fountain of truth witnesses in Psalm 104) is carried out by angels who are most powerful in strength. 

Again, when heat is emitted through the mediation of the Word with the angels administering, the air—having been reduced by contrary blasts into vapors and watery clouds, and changed by the cold blast into snow, hail, ice, and frost—is again resolved into drops of water. This is clear from the conclusion of the last testimony cited from the Psalmist, for it follows in verse 18: "He sends out his word and melts them; as soon as he breathes his word, the waters flow." From this we argue that by the emission of the Word—that is, of divine light—and the South wind blowing by its power with the Angels ministering, those things which the cold North wind [Aquilo] congealed, the South wind [Auster] dissolves back into that which it was before. 

Moreover, that watery vapor is dissolved into air (as into its first matter from which it originally arose) by the action of heat; no one commonly experienced in decoctions <note>Decoction: The process of boiling a substance in water to extract its essence; the author uses this as a laboratory analogy for how heat turns liquid back into "air" or vapor.</note> can deny this. Therefore, cold condenses the air, but heat subtilizes <note>Subtilizes: To make something "subtle" or thin, like turning a liquid into a gas.</note> it. Yet, the cause of this condensation and thinning is always brought about with the winds and their qualities assisting. By their opposition, the air between them is compressed and first reduced into the form of vapor, and then into a watery smoke or cloudy substance. This happens especially if a hot and moist wind (the southern) contends against a cold and dry wind (the northern). 

For it is necessary that the watery or moist mass of air—from which rains are generated—or the dry mass—bringing forth hail and snow—should be procreated in the interval or aerial medium between these opposite blasts, according to which opposing wind is dominant. However, where the North wind [Aquilo] blows and the South wind [Auster] does not oppose it (or only slightly), there ice, frost, and rime are produced from the condensation and constriction of the air and waters. Similarly, when the South wind blows, if the North wind does not oppose it, we see that the sky does not abound so much with clouds, nor is the air so damp; but since the northern wind rarely rests, there are also rarely southern winds that are not accompanied by clouds and rains. 

We say, therefore, that the nature of uniform air is fit by accident to take on any disposition of the winds. When the North wind [Borea] blows from the North [Aquilone], it congeals and thickens the air itself; it gathers and glues its dispersed parts by its dryness, and its coldness coagulates and thickens them. Thus (as is clear in snow, frost, and hail), the wind converts the air into an earthy condition. But when the South wind [Austro] blows from the South [Meridie], that wind conversely converts that portion of the air which the North wind made earthy back into water, since the works of cold are destroyed and dissolved by heat. Again, the hot and dry spirits of the East wind [Eurus] convert that water into an aerial or fiery disposition, which the West wind [Occidentalis] nourishes and refreshes with its breath. Those most skilled in the mystery of the Magnet have also discovered that the earth has its own poles, its own circles, a Zodiac, an Equinoctial, Solstitial, and Polar lines. <note>This refers to 16th and 17th-century magnetic philosophy (such as that of William Gilbert), which argued the Earth was a giant magnet with a "soul" that mirrored the celestial spheres.</note> From this it follows that the winds do not fall silent within its internal spirit from their own regions any differently than those winds from the regions of the world or the open air; but we acknowledge that such particular winds depend upon those universal ones, as we shall show more clearly in the following sections.

Consequently, the bodies which are, so to speak, bathed indiscriminately by these particular airs follow the conditions of the airs enclosed within them; they are altered by their temperateness or intemperateness. From this, philosophers and physicians have concluded (and quite maturely so) that the temperament of the body follows the temperament of the soul. <note>original: "temperatura corporis sequatur & temperaturam animæ"; a core principle of Galenic medicine, linking physical health to the "spirits" of the soul.</note> Thus it is that when the internal spirit is disturbed by the external—whether by heat, cold, moisture, or dryness—the body in which it resides is also disturbed by those same afflictions. From these things, therefore, it is clearly declared that since the entire mass of sublunary air is affected by a multiform kind of meteors (whether wholesome or unwholesome), it is necessary that the particular air of the giant creature that is the Earth, as well as that of the tiny creature that is Man, be affected in the same way. Indeed, when the terrestrial spirit is infected by the mundane spirit, we see that the spirit of man participates in those same passions. And this is why famine, plague, and pestilential fevers are, for the most part, inseparable companions. Hence it is said that when a comet reigns, famine and plague are foretold; for famine proves the sterility of the earth and the impurity and poisonousness of its fruits (by which the spirits are nourished), as well as the corruption of the universal spirit. Thus it happens that the human spirit also suffers from the corrupted universal spirit drawn in through inhalation, and also from the terrestrial spirit by way of nutrition. Indeed, sometimes the particular air is infected by the tainted breath of the earth, as occasionally appears during an earthquake, which a plague follows. And what is more, we say reciprocally that the human spirit, by its own error, corrupted that terrestrial spirit. Thus it came to pass that because of the sin of Adam, not only man but also the earth itself (which GOD ordained from the beginning for the sons of men) was cursed and became fatal to man himself; but concerning these things, we shall speak more abundantly in the following sections.

# On the Material Cause of Meteors. 33

## CHAPTER VIII.

### On the three stages in the movement of augmentation and growth between simple air and meteorological bodies (or imperfectly mixed bodies), and on their mathematical reasoning.

In the last chapter of the preceding booklet, you have seen it declared that progress was made from nothing, or from the womb of matter <note>original: "hylæ gremio"; "Hyle" is a Greek term used by alchemists and Neoplatonists to describe the primordial, unformed substance of the universe.</note>, through the emanation of light toward unity. By the revelation of this light, another potential unity was produced, opposite to it in disposition—namely, darkness. Thus, the progression moved from the monad <note>The number one, representing unity or God.</note> to the dyad <note>The number two, representing duality or opposition.</note>, and from the dyad to the triad, through the introduction and production of the humid spirit. This spirit acts as a glue <note>original: "gluten"</note> between these two, joining both extremes together like a soul with a body. Finally, all these progress toward the number four <note>the quaternary</note>, reaching the completion of the simple world by bringing into act the four elements, which differ from one another. These elements are the immediate beginnings of all mixtures, just as in geometry, square surfaces are the immediate principles of a cubic body. This order we have depicted arithmetically as follows:

<note>A diagram illustrates the metaphysical transition from light to matter. At the center is a point labeled "a. Light" from which rays emanate. †. Absolute Darkness. 
a. Light, the first creature.

e. Fire. 
f. Air. 
g. e. Water: 4. Earth: Root. 2. Square. 4.

Where the binary number <note>The number two.</note> is the material root from which the first square (4), indicating the elements, is derived. Likewise, in the production of perfectly mixed bodies, just as many stages intervene in the movement of nature—from the square (the four elements) to the cube (the perfectly mixed "elementated" body <note>In alchemy, an "elementated" body is one where the four elements have combined to form a complex substance like a mineral, plant, or animal.</note>). All these intervening stages ought truly to be called "imperfectly mixed bodies," insofar as they progress from the simplicity of the elements toward a complete mixture. In this order, the number 4 relates to a perfectly mixed body <note>In traditional alchemy, a "perfectly mixed body" is a stable substance where the four elements are so thoroughly combined they cannot be easily separated, such as a metal or a living creature.</note> in the same way that 1 (or light in a simple progression) relates to the 4 elements. Furthermore, just as the number 2 represents prime matter and form, from which the four elements were multiplied and brought forth, so too do the four elements denote matter and form within the simplicity of the elements. From these, through further multiplication, mixed bodies proceed, becoming more perfect the more deeply that original Unity immerses itself into the multitude of matter.

Therefore, just as the luminous unity (1) is the simplest source of all simple things, so also are the four elements the simplest origin of mixed bodies. In this progression of mixtures, the fifth order relates to the fourth as the number 2 relates to nothingness (or darkness) among simple things. Similarly, the sixth order relates to the fifth as 2 to 1; the seventh to the sixth as 3 to 2; and finally, the eighth to the seventh as 4 to 3.

Thus, as we see in the first progression—where the number 2 was made by the shining forth of the 1—so the four elements, by clustering themselves together in the "womb of the air" (which is their parent, the universal spirit of the world), produce the first species of mixture. From these come the winds and invisible "meteors," <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and clouds, not just falling stars.</note> whether fiery or watery. These gradually thicken through the power of the winds or take on a visible fiery nature, which is indicated by the sixth order. This corresponds to the number 3 in the simple progression, wherein water is either brilliantly illuminated by light (denoting fiery meteors in the second degree of mixture) or water prevails over light (indicating thunderous meteors). Finally, the seventh degree shows more dense and dark meteors, such as clouds of hail, snow, and rain. If these continue further into composition, they coalesce into perfectly mixed bodies.

For it must be known for certain that all bodies—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—are nothing other than clouds or meteors brought to a state of perfect mixture. For who can doubt that every perfectly mixed thing was first imperfectly mixed? It is necessary that imperfection stands between the simple elements and the completely composed bodies; it is impossible to find two extremes where the middle ground between the starting point and the destination is missing. We observe this even in the movement toward generation: the seed <note>original: "sperma"</note> is a kind of imperfect mixture, like a mist or "little cloud of generation," which proceeds steadily through natural motion until it reaches the complete production of the fetus or the perfect mixture.

We say, therefore, that a "meteor" is called an imperfect mixture because it is "on the way" <note>original: "in via"</note>; it is in a state of natural motion, having arisen from the simple elements in the womb of the air and tending toward the goal of perfection for its species. If, due to some impediment in its path, it fails in its motion and cannot progress further toward perfection, it gradually returns to its simple nature from which it was first derived. If it is procreated by poisonous winds or malevolent spirits blowing together, it then mostly infects the air and brings a bad omen. But if it is procreated by benevolent breaths by divine will, it sometimes purges and cleanses the air, bringing a good and propitious omen to the earth and its fruits; it is even proved to be healthy for the lives of animals, if God so wills.

Nor should it be doubted that meteors contribute to the production of perfectly mixed things. We are taught by experience that frogs, worms, and monstrous animals—likewise flesh, blood, grain, and other crops, and even stones, sand, and dust—have fallen from the clouds and the air by the blowing of the winds, things truly worthy of wonder. It must therefore be understood that there are meteors of both generation and corruption.

Whether they be healthy or unhealthy, meteors of contrary conditions—namely, those of generation <note>The process of coming into being or growing.</note> and corruption <note>The process of decay or breaking down.</note>—are always moved by contrary motions. For those things which lead toward corruption move backward toward the principles from which they first progressed. Indeed, if they overcome the strength of the "perfectly mixed" nature to which they join themselves, they drag that nature backward with them through the path of resolution <note>The breaking down of a complex substance into its simpler components.</note>. In the manner of a toxin, they change that nature into their own, as is clearly explained every day by the pestilential seeds dispersed everywhere by the spirit of poisonous meteors. 

You will find this kind of motion, pertaining to both generation and corruption, most excellently and clearly described by us in Section 1, Part 2, Part 3, Chapter 5 of our *Theosophical, Cabalistical, and Physiological Discourse of Both Worlds*, where we treat the earthly principles. Nevertheless, we have provided a visual demonstration of that passage here.

For a further demonstration of this, I commend to you the place named before. Although I mentioned there the progression in generation from the root 2 into the square 4, and from that into the cube 8, and again the regression in corruption from the cube 8 to the square 4, and from that square to the root 2; yet, so that you may rightly understand my mind in this matter, I wish you first to know: when I mentioned generation there, I understood the linear progression of the creation of man and his derivation from the primary light and darkness. By the motion of corruption from 8 to 2, I intended the return of the human creature into his primary principles from which he first proceeded. 

This regression is not to be expected before the final *Pereat* <note>Latin: "Let it perish," referring to the Last Judgment or the final dissolution of the material world.</note>, in which even the elements are to be reduced back into their primary simples <note>The basic, indivisible building blocks of reality, such as pure fire or pure water, before they are mixed into the world we see.</note>. However, in the common alteration of this world, whether toward generation or corruption, the transition occurs only from the square (acting as the ultimate simples from which the world consists) to the cube, or the regression from the cube back to the square. This is because the simple elements themselves cannot be corrupted; only composites <note>Things made of multiple elements joined together.</note> can, as they are constituted from contrary natures. For if the elements were liable to be resolved into their primary principles, then the world itself would be subject to total corruption, as it is forged and filled by the binding of elements and the airy spirit. 

But now I shall proceed to the description of the **formal cause** <note>The "formal cause" refers to the design, shape, or soul of a thing—the "idea" that makes it what it is—as opposed to the "material cause" or the physical stuff it is made of.</note> of meteors, since we have spoken abundantly enough (as we believe) in this book regarding their **material cause**.

**BOOK THREE**

**Division I.**

***On the Formal Cause of Meteors.***

**Chapter I of Division I.**

***A precise treatment of the formal cause of the meteors of both worlds, as well as their various distinctions.***

Since in the preceding book we have discussed, more than sufficiently (as it seems to us), the material origin of the meteors <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, rainbows, and comets, not just falling stars.</note> of both worlds, it is my intention in this place—for the sake of a more certain method—to discourse upon their formal cause <note>The "formal cause" is a philosophical term referring to the design, shape, or essential nature that makes a thing what it is.</note>, albeit briefly and succinctly. We have already declared that the material cause of meteors is that out of which they are formed as a substantial part—namely, a substrate of thinner air, more or less contracted and compressed according to the condition of the meteor. In the same way, we now affirm that their formal cause is that by which those meteors claim a name and a peculiar essence for themselves. 

Through this form, they are carved out or delineated from the universal and invisible mass of the world’s air and brought into visible existence. This form clothes and shapes this or that aerial vapor into various and diverse figures that differ from one another. This diversity of images or shapes is taught to arise from the hidden and internal form of the meteors. It is no different than how the external image or figure of a man—proceeding from his own internal essence—causes his structure to differ from that of other animals and plants. It is by this form that we recognize from a distance that a certain being is a man, and not a beast or a plant. 

By a clearly similar reasoning or distinction, we gather and distinguish a dark meteor from a bright one—that is, one species from another. And again, in a more specific respect, we distinguish one bright thing from another bright thing, and one opaque or dark thing from another dark thing. For example, we observe that a comet, a lightning bolt, a "fiery lance," or a burning column is distinguished and differs from a cloud, a mist, a halo, or dew. Even within the same category or species, we see a comet vary by the same formal difference from a burning column or from lightning. Similarly, in the dark region, even the common eye discerns that a cloud differs from a mist, a mist from dew, and rain from frost, and so on.

Hence it is that in this treatise of ours, by means of these formal causes, we distribute meteors first into their genera, then those into their species, and finally those—after various subdivisions—into infinite individuals. We see this partitioned no differently than the trunk of a tree into branches, and those again into subdivided twigs, which finally terminate in small shoots, so that you may reach the goal of our intention by an easier method.

And since our purpose in this present treatise leads us to compare the meteors of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World," referring to the universe and the natural environment.</term> with those of the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: The "Little World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</term>—or man himself—so that we may more clearly demonstrate the reason for his health or illness through the effects of the good or bad meteors generated within him, therefore, throughout the whole thread of this progression of ours, after each chapter on the meteors of the Macrocosm, we have made a correlation and comparison. We apply the members of the preceding chapter to those of the Microcosm or man, specifically by linking the meteors, humors, and properties of the one to those of the other, as the subject and the occasion for treatment present themselves.

We find it written, and not without wisdom, by Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, a series of texts foundational to alchemy and Western esotericism.</note>, a most profound priest, that the world belongs to God, but man is the son and image of the world. For just as God originally created the substance of the world out of nothing, so also He fashioned man from the matter of the world already created; specifically, his external part from the mud of the earth <note>original: "limo terrae"</note>, but his internal part from the worldly spirit—which had been previously adorned as a most precious gift with the divine breath <note>original: "spiraculo"</note>, through the forms of the reason and intellect of God. From this, therefore, we observe that just as the great house or vessel of the Macrocosmic spirit is the opaque earth—without which no perfectly mixed thing in the sublunary <term>sublunary</term> <note>Literally "under the moon," referring to the earthly realm where things are subject to change, unlike the "perfect" heavens.</note> world can be brought to completion (for the earth is the <term>matrix</term> <note>A source or "womb" where something is generated.</note> of the worldly elements as well as the celestial and even super-celestial influences)—likewise it can be hidden from no one that the human spirit claims for itself a similar receptacle. This spirit is a receptacle or vehicle for celestial and super-celestial inflows in no other way than the elemental air is in the Macrocosm. From this it is clear how great, close, and necessary a relationship exists between these two spirits and both of these bodies—namely, those of the Macrocosm and Microcosm. Indeed, since both the spirit and the body of the "lesser world" <note>The Microcosm, or human being.</note> are derived from those of the "greater world" <note>The Macrocosm, or universe.</note>, it must follow infallibly that both the airy and ethereal spirit in man, as well as his own opaque body, are sustained and nourished by the world. They remain in their state and existence at every moment and adhere to the worldly parts—both spiritual and bodily—by an inviolable bond, such that they cannot be separated from one another even by death or the dissolution of the composite being. This is why, from the beginning, when the elements of the greater world become sick, the airy and terrestrial parts of man are also very quickly infected, as will be described more accurately in the following pages.

**Wind is an invisible spirit or air, animated and quickened by divine light from the face or sight of Jehovah, like a breath proceeding from His nostrils, to execute His pleasure both in the heavens and on the earth.**

Or thus:
**Wind is a certain angelic spirit; or subtle air inspired and animated by the fiery spirit of Jehovah—sometimes visible and manifest, as in lightning and thunderbolts, and sometimes invisible and hidden, as in that which is heard but not at all seen—sent forth from some region of the world by divine and secret means to execute the divine will, whether for salvation and benevolence, or for punishment and malediction upon the earth.**

Or thus:

**Wind is a certain angelic creature, produced by Jehovah the Creator, composed of air as its agitated matter and inspired by divine light as its moving central soul; brought forth from His treasures at His will, it is sent here and there, either for beneficence and mercy, or for a scourge and punishment.**

Or thus:
**Wind is an angelic spirit, breathing here and there secretly and invisibly according to the abstruse good pleasure of the Creator; though its noise may be heard, the boundary of where it comes from or where it goes is unknown to mortals.** *John 3:8. The Spirit breathes where it wills, and a man hears its voice, but he knows not whence it comes or whither it goes.* Furthermore, the sacred writings testify that the way and place of God are unknown to men.

Or thus, therefore, from the mouth of the Savior:
**Wind is a spirit that breathes where it wills; although its voice is heard, yet the goal is unknown, and the place is uncertain from whence it comes or whither it goes.**

Or thus, as we perceive or gather from the passages cited above:
**Winds are the angels of God, most mighty in strength, performing His word, hearkening to the voice of His speech; His flaming ministers, doing His pleasure.** <note>Psalm 103 and 104</note>

Here, therefore, we see how opposed that **Pagan doctrine** <note>Referring to Aristotle's natural philosophy</note> is to this one, which is drawn from the fountain of all truth. From this it follows that he who adheres firmly to the Aristotelian doctrine cannot fundamentally dwell within the Christian faith. *No man (says our Savior) can faithfully serve two masters*, and St. Paul advises us not without reason *to abstain from vain philosophy*; for in truth, that is the chief instrument or organ of the Devil himself, by which he is accustomed to distract worldly men from God and to draw them toward his own antipathetic harmony by sophisticated deceits, inciting them to give faith to his otherwise vain temptations. This, therefore, is the reason why the men of this age, who are [not] masters of the divine mind, forgetting their illustrious origin and nobility—as if led by illusions and the lights of darkness—are so crude and unskilled both in true **theosophy** <term>theosophy: direct divine wisdom or knowledge of God</term> and in the sincere arts, that they understand neither God as He truly is, nor His creatures...

## On the Formal Cause of Meteors. 47

...they seem to comprehend [this] by this common term: *With a West wind (says Moses) in its strength, God carried away the locusts, Exodus 10.* <note>original: "Vento ab Occidente (inquit Moyſes) in ſuo robore DEVS ſuſtulit locuſtas, Exod. 10."</note>

Nor indeed is it without cause that we, in the division of the Cardinal winds, made mention of the poles and the equinoctial circle, and consequently of the winds blowing from them both on earth and in heaven. For we are taught by the experience of the magnetic stone (which is also called a <term>terella</term> <note>From the Latin for "little earth," a *terella* is a magnetized sphere used by early modern scientists to model the Earth's magnetic field.</note>) that the earth itself holds an excellent proportion to the heavens of the world and its circles. We also learn that the earth lives and breathes in imitation of its parents—the heavens—by means of an aerial spirit, mediated by that mundane spirit from its four quarters, just as the heaven does. The human body is seen to emulate this in every way, as one who possesses his own poles, circles, and winds proper to each of his four quarters, insofar as he is a "son of the world," just as has been explained in our <note>The author is likely referring to his own work, *Anatomia Amphitheatrum*, which treats the human body as a symbolic map of the universe.</note> mystical Anatomy.

The experiment of the magnetic <term>terella</term>, by whose disposition we are also accustomed to judge the nature of the Macrocosmic <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> and Microcosmic <note>The "Small World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> earth, is of this kind:

First, it is certain and proven by experience that the magnetic *terella* sends out its powers from its center into a sphere; and this same thing is undoubtedly observed in the earth, of which the magnet is a tiny offspring. The magnet possesses the disposition of the whole no differently than any drop of water possesses the nature of the great sea. For in the center of the earth is a **central Sun**, possessing within itself an exactly magnetic force by which it draws its like to itself. Indeed, just as we observe two poles in the mathematical heaven which rotate the machine of the world, so too do we find natural poles, endowed with <term>Macrocosmic virtue</term> <note>Universal or celestial power.</note>, in the terrestrial globe. One of these tends toward the Arctic pole, and the other declines toward the opposite part of the world. This can be most easily demonstrated by the nature of a round magnet (which is a small portion of the earth, no different than a drop of water is to the element of water). When this stone is shaped into a spherical form like the earth, it indicates through its effects not only the poles, but also the equator and other circular lines at various latitudes from each other. For the closer the parts of the magnetic sphere are to its equator, the more obliquely the magnetic iron (the needle) will be seen to be attracted and lured to it. But the parts of the spherical body are observed to draw the iron or needle to themselves more directly the closer they are to the pole. We have expressed the figure of the spherical stone with its various formulas of attraction here.

<note>A circular diagram illustrates a "terella" or spherical magnet. A vertical line through the center is labeled "Axis," and a horizontal line is labeled "Aequa" (Equator). Various iron needles are drawn around the circumference; those near the "Aequa" lay flat or tilt slightly, while those near the poles stand upright, demonstrating how magnetic inclination changes with latitude.</note>

A similar magnetic force is also present in the human body, which is also a *terella*. The magnetic spirit of the human is observed to be so strong that the Sages were not ignorant of how to attract not only elementary but even celestial virtues in a certain admirable way, and to join terrestrial things with celestial ones through this magnetic faculty of spirits. Indeed, just as a pure and clean spirit is able to attract clean things to itself from the heavens and elements, so also a malignant and impure spirit, by the opposite reasoning, attracts spirits similar to itself from the heavens and the earths—namely, the good attracts divine inspirations, while the evil attracts diabolical ones. And by this kind of magnetic virtue of spirits, not only those most skilled in natural magic but even witches themselves are accustomed to produce things so stupendous and scarcely imaginable, who by a hidden mastery of this kind are accustomed to malignantly infect the spirits of men from a distance.

### **The Relation or application of the aforesaid Macrocosmic distinction to the human microcosm.**

The same must also be said regarding the cardinal winds of the body—or the "human earth"—as was said of those of the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note>. We therefore divide the <term>Microcosmic</term> <note>The "Small World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> winds in this manner:

Just as we see the earth (following the example of the magnetic <term>terella</term> <note>A small spherical magnet used to model the Earth's magnetic properties.</note>) contain its own quarters of the world—namely the Poles, the Equinoctial, and the Tropics—so indeed the "little earth" of the human body undoubtedly possesses within itself its own quarters and principal regions. The various spirits of these regions attract the mundane spirit to themselves in different ways through a magnetic virtue. 

From this, it follows that just as different parts are found in iron which, by the property of their essence and a certain natural inclination, seek out one part of a magnet or another (as is clearly shown in the experiment mentioned above), so too in the mundane spirit attracted into the human body through inspiration [breathing], one may find various parts that—by their condition and nature—naturally adhere more to this or that portion of the human body's spirit. 

For example, that portion of the mundane spirit introduced into the human body through breathing has some northern parts, some southern, others eastern, and finally some western. But in its general inclination, it participates more in that wind whose dominion was strongest at the time it was inhaled. Thus it happens that a certain spirit or wind renders a person's spirits more fluid and liable to <term>catarrhs</term> <note>A buildup of mucus in the nose or throat, often associated with "moist" or southern winds in early medicine.</note>—namely, the Southern wind. So it is with the others: even the spirit attracted at the first birth (or rather, at the hour of the fetus's life) causes it to have a phlegmatic, melancholic, sanguine, or choleric complexion, according to the nature of the wind first inhaled at that time. 

Similarly, the spirit of natural life is derived from all the winds (as Ezekiel seems to assert, who prophesied to the bones saying, *“Come, O spirit, from the four winds, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live”* <note>original: "Adueni ô ſpiritus à quatuor ventis, & inſuffla iſtos mortuos vt viuant"</note>). From the inhaled Macrocosmic spirit, it divides those parts proper to each wind of the Macrocosm and distributes them into its own quarters in the "human earth" by magnetic virtue. That is, the northern part of the Microcosmic spirit is attracted by the northern part of the Macrocosmic spirit, both for its preservation and to perform those duties in the human body which must be fulfilled by the cold and <term>styptic</term> <note>A substance or quality that contracts tissues or stops bleeding; here associated with the "dry/cold" nature of the North and Melancholy.</note> temperament of that part—namely, to restore the Melancholic humor, the food of the Spleen. 

In the same way, its southern portion performs this same duty in the sanguine office for the preservation of the liver and the creation of blood. Likewise, the portion destined for life performs its work in the heart and arteries. For like things always rejoice in like things, and by a certain magnetic attraction, they embrace each other closely in the bonds of love, because "nature rejoices in nature" and desires it. 

Have we not experienced and proven this most exactly in the "anatomy" of Wheat and Bread? In that process, we divided the matter into its distinct elements, which we found to be nothing other than wind and ether when examined by the test of fire; for by the application of a very gentle heat, they were dissolved into smoke very similar to atoms. From these things we can argue—and clearly so—that a composite body stands in relation to its internal animating spirit as a cloud does to the wind. For just as a cloud was previously air, which is condensed into mist and cloud by the breath of opposing winds, so indeed the opaque composite body was nothing but a cloud reduced into a perfect mixture by the benevolent breath of the winds. 

This is proven in this way: namely, because every thing is resolved back into that from which it was primordially created. But wood, wheat, and the animal body are reduced by the violence of fire into smoke or thick vapor (acting like a cloud), which is also gradually dissipated into invisible air, from which air all things are seen to depart. Thus is verified that axiom of Plato: *From that on which the principle of any thing depends, in the same will be its increase.* <note>original: "A quo dependet alicuius rei principium, in eodem erit ſuum incrementum"</note> Since no creature deprived of air can either grow or live, we say therefore that the whole composite body is nothing other than air of various conditions, gathered together into that which it is.

By these things, therefore, it is clearly explained that in the Spleen there is a magnetic force which attracts to itself those things—both from nourishment and from the air drawn in through breath—which are of a northern nature; in the liver, those which participate in the southern winds; in the heart, those which, by the natural power of life, are descending from the ether; in the gallbladder, those from the bilious winds, such as the <term>Eurus</term> and <term>Caecias</term> <note>The Northeast wind.</note>; and finally, in the stomach and viscera, those which receive their life from the western winds. From these effects of the parts of man, therefore, we can gather the points of the poles and the equinoctials (both eastern and western), no differently than we gather the equinox, poles, and vertical axis of a magnet through the effect of applying iron to its parts, as in the experiment previously described. Is it not also established by a similar reasoning that, from the application of various winds, air is converted into a cloud, containing within itself bodies of diverse nature, namely stones, flames, waters, and so on?

contagious, it most easily absorbs and nourishes the "seeds of meteors" <note>The author uses "meteors" to refer to any atmospheric phenomenon, including winds and vapors, which he believes also exist inside the body as gases.</note> of that same wind; hence, such people are infected more quickly and more lethally by this kind of plague or epidemic disease than others. And this doctrine of ours seems not to differ or disagree much from that of Galen and Hippocrates, who both arrive at this opinion: namely, that **Bilious** types <note>People with a "choleric" temperament, thought to be hot and dry.</note> endure the hot temperature of summer with greater difficulty, but fare better in the winter and northern cold; conversely, **phlegmatic** types <note>People thought to be cold and moist.</note> tolerate the Southern, rainy, and wintry disposition with greater difficulty, while the summer state is more pleasing to them. Their words are these: *In summer* (says Hippocrates, Aphorisms book 3, 18), *the elderly are healthier, as they are naturally cold.* And Galen, commenting on that passage: *In the elderly, because of the coldness of their temperament, summer is most beneficial.* And elsewhere: *Those prone to phlegm fare best in summer; those prone to bile fare best in winter.*

Do we not also have this confirmed in the blowing of the world’s winds, in which the **Northern** winds seem to cure and root out the effects of the **Southern** ones? For just as the condition of the Southern wind is to produce clouds, dissolve frozen things, thicken the air, and produce rains—and even to generate contagious diseases—so indeed the spirit of the North wind dissipates clouds or freezes those already dissolved, thins the air, drives away rains, and opposes the growth of the plague. So also, when the dry blasts of the **Spleen** predominate, thin vapors and flowing rheums <note>Mucus or watery discharge.</note> are thickened, frozen, and halted. Similarly, the vapor sent out from the **Liver** dissolves those things frozen and condensed by the blasts of the Spleen, and opens the pores constricted and locked by them; and so it goes with the rest. 

But although we write these things having been taught by effect and common experience—as if by a "demonstration from the effect" <note>original: "demonstratione à posteriori"; reasoning from known consequences to unknown causes.</note>—nevertheless, the reason for this matter is deeply hidden and mystical, which can only be indicated by a "demonstration from the cause" <note>original: "demonstratione à priori"; reasoning from theoretical causes to effects.</note>. For there are winds of health and mercy, and there are also winds of unhealthiness and severity; there are also great angels or Archangels who are ordained by God to preside over these winds, and they send out their legions either for vengeance and punishment, or for beneficence, according to the good pleasure of their Creator (in whose presence they stand). There is also a certain universal angel, the first emanation from the brightness of the Almighty—called **Wisdom** by the book of Ecclesiasticus, **Metattron** by the Kabbalists, and the **Messiah** and **Soter** (Savior) by the mystics—in whose power it is to preserve men from the violence of the Wind-Demons <note>original: "Cacodaemonum Ventosorum".</note>. He, I say, is the very solar soul, the presiding officer of life and health, acting kindly toward the preservation of health in no different a way than the office of **Raphael** is ordained to drive away diseases (as is evident from the etymology of his name <note>The name Raphael means "God heals" in Hebrew.</note>). He is the one who "ascended from the rising of the Sun, having the seal of the living GOD, and crying with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying, 'Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads'" (Revelation 7). 

But concerning this mystical method of inflicting disease or preserving health, we shall—God willing—discuss more flowingly in our treatise on the *Metaphysics of Meteors*, regarding both healthy and unhealthy causes. However, you will find the history of the **Microcosmic winds** described and treated more fully and extensively in our treatise on *Mystical Anatomy*, of which you nevertheless have a visual demonstration depicted here.

### Chapter I. Of Member II.

#### Where we treat meteorological bodies produced from winds in general.

The condition of meteorological bodies, in both substance and form, is the same as those perfectly mixed things which were previously imperfectly mixed bodies in their movement away from aerial simplicity; in this state, they took on the form of "meteorological bodies," namely between the *starting point* <note>original: "terminus a quo"</note>, which is the purely aerial state, and the *destination* <note>original: "terminus ad quem"</note>, namely perfect composition: as you have had sufficiently demonstrated in the preceding sections. From these things it seems to stand clearly enough that everything that exists, regarding its consistency, is originally nothing but one and the same thing, namely air; and that there is nothing composite in the world unless it is either a meteor or derived from a meteor. It is a "meteor" (I say) if it is an imperfect body, and "from a meteor" because it is through that nature that a transition must necessarily occur from a simple nature to a perfectly composite one. 

For it is impossible for a progression from a starting point to a destination to occur unless a middle state is interposed. Indeed, no perfection is found in the number two <note>The "dyad," often associated in Pythagorean thought with division and instability.</note>, since it possesses only two terms; for this reason, the Pythagoreans called it, not without reason, a "confused and imperfect number." Therefore, they most rightly attributed the dignity of perfection to the number three, because in it three terms are found: the beginning, the middle, and the end. These terms in composition are like an imperfectly mixed or meteorological body. Thus we see dough formed from impalpable flour as if from air, serving as the middle term or the "composition in mid-motion" between the bread and the flour; then, by the reduction of moisture and by cooking and the hardening of that imperfect composite, it is brought back into the perfect form of bread. Does it not also appear in the testing of wood, or animal bodies, or even metals such as lead, iron, copper, etc., in the crucible or cupel <note>A shallow ceramic cup used in assaying or alchemy to separate precious metals from base metals.</note>, that those bodies are first converted by the violence of fire into a thick smoke or a cloud...

### Chapter 2. Member 2.

#### On the principal parts in composition, and first concerning Light.

Since it is certain and beyond all doubt that two things are required for the constitution of bodies—both meteorological and "perfectly mixed" <note>A "perfect mixture" refers to a stable, solid substance (like a mineral or plant) where the elements are fully combined, as opposed to "imperfect mixtures" like clouds or rain which easily disperse.</note>—I believe it will be worthwhile to diligently inquire into the nature of these two things. But since it is impossible for anything to be produced in the nature of things without action (which belongs to the "form") and passion (which belongs to the "matter"), we must inspect the natures of these two in composition, as without them nothing in the world can exist. 

We find that **Form** is a single, simple thing, the primary act, central, the agent, the offspring of primary light, forming and effecting all things. It is supernatural and uncreated in its origin, but clothed in natural spirit and effect, it becomes natural and created. Hence Ecclesiasticus says: *Wisdom is the first creature* <note>original: "Sapientia est prima creatura." Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 1:4.</note>. And because light was created on the first day, it is thus considered as one—specifically in respect to the "garment of the spiritual world" which it puts on. It is called an "Angel" in respect to the soul being simply formal; or, in respect to the great name of GOD inscribed in the Angel, it is *Jehovah*, the immediate emanation of GOD (the fountain of light) into the world, through which His spirit (previously existing only in potential) was given form. 

And so it is said that light was created on the first day—that is, the spirit shining with divine light, or the divine act, was clothed in the spiritual substance of the world, which was illuminated by its presence. Whence it was said by David, *GOD is clothed in light* <note>Psalm 104:2</note>, meaning the illuminated spirit, or the glory of GOD shining in His creature. Likewise, in His wrath, GOD is called a "consuming fire." And this light or "form" sometimes assumes the name of its garment; hence we find it written: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day and a starry light by night* <note>original: "Sapientia fuit Israelitis tegumentum interdiu & lux stellaris nocte." Wisdom of Solomon 10:17.</note>, and elsewhere, *I, Wisdom, came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth like a mist, my throne was in a pillar of cloud, etc.* <note>Ecclesiasticus 24:3-4.</note>

Therefore, this divine Wisdom is the "act of actions" and the central mover in every creature; as the wise man said: *The incorruptible spirit of GOD is in every thing* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 12:1</note>. Indeed, this luminous spirit of GOD is the central virtue of the thing itself, without which it can neither live nor exist. That this spirit of Wisdom is the innermost light of meteors and the "soul of souls"—indeed, the secret mystical soul of anything, whether imperfect or perfect—is evident from three points: 
1. In its perfection, it surpasses all things, being divine, incorruptible, and uncreated. 
2. It is more mobile than all moving things, simpler and more subtle than any spirit, and more powerful than any act. 
3. It is in every thing, as has been said—that is, in every element and every "elementated" <note>A thing composed of the four elements.</note> object. 

This can also be easily gathered from the words of the previously cited text: *I, Wisdom, covered the earth like a mist, my throne is in a pillar of cloud, I alone circled the circuit of the heavens, and I walked in the depth of the abyss, in the waves of the sea and in all the earth and in every people and nation I rested.* Therefore, divine Wisdom—which the wise man clearly describes with these words—is the holy spirit of intelligence: unique or simple, manifold, subtle, undefiled, certain, sweet, free from passion, sharp, kind, humane, possessing all virtues, overseeing all things, containing all intelligible spirits, more mobile than all moving things, reaching everywhere because of its purity, a vapor or emanation of the power or brightness of God. Since it is one, it can do all things, and remaining in itself, it renews all things, transferring itself through every generation <note>Wisdom of Solomon 7:22-27.</note>. 

I say that this is the central life or principle and the most internal "being" of any thing existing in this world. It is not that fictitious or imaginary "form" of Aristotle, which makes things "imaginable" by attributing everything to its own nature and not immediately to GOD. *By the Word,* says the Evangelist, *all things were made, and without him nothing; in him was life and that was the light of men, the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.* <note>John 1:3-10.</note> 

How foolish, then, is that distinction made by Christian philosophers, who wish to distinguish and separate GOD from His power and virtue, saying that GOD is everywhere "virtually" (by His power) but not "essentially." It is as if any sane or self-consistent person would say that the virtue of GOD could be separated or divided from His essence any more than the solar rays can be separated from the sun itself, which are in every way inseparable. This is also confirmed by Hermes Mercurius Trismegistus in *Pimander*, Book 12: *Mind is indeed of the very essence of GOD, if indeed he has an essence; it is born from it, and therefore is by no means divided from the essence of GOD, but rather connected to it in the same way that light is to the body of the Sun.* This "Worldly Mind" is that immediate emanation, the brightness of eternal light, the spotless mirror of the divine majesty and the image of His goodness, through which we know GOD from His "posterior" parts—that is, in His creatures. It is that very Wisdom which we described above through the testimony of Holy Scripture.

As we also have confirmed in the same text of **Wisdom 7**. Concerning this, **Trismegistus** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom a vast body of "Hermetic" wisdom on philosophy, alchemy, and magic was attributed.</note> speaks from the revelation of his own good spirit: *The Mind, the soul of God, rules over all things, and even over law and all the rest; nothing of those things which pertain to fate is impossible for the mind: Poimandres 12.* Therefore, the human mind is superior to fate, yet it does not neglect those things which are subject to fate. This Mind, then, is that from which all souls of the entire world receive their life and their being, no differently than from one candle, countless candles are lit and receive their own life, as it were. Whence the aforementioned Teacher <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus</note> says: *Universal souls throughout the whole world flow forth from the single soul of the whole world, as if distributed and running about; of these souls, however, there are many changes, partly indeed for the better and more happily, and partly into the contrary: Poimandres 10.* And this same thing does not seem to differ from the Sacred Letters, where it is left written: *That God created all things through Jesus Christ, Ephesians 3:9.* and elsewhere, *he who had first descended to the deep parts of the earth ascended, and he who descended is that very one who ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fulfill all things in this way, Ephesians 4:8.* and also *the spirit of wisdom (says Solomon) fills the whole world, Wisdom 1.* Furthermore, it is said: *God made the thick clouds his vehicle and his pavilion, Psalm 104:3 and Job 22.* Therefore, this sort of luminous act of God is present everywhere in the air by his presence, even if it is not manifested to the eye. Thus also *in the sun he placed his tabernacle.* Finally, this divine power or essence is present everywhere, as the Royal Psalmist testifies: *namely, in heaven, in hell, in the furthest parts of the sea, in the night, in the darkness, Psalm 139:7.* Hence it is said: *know therefore and recall to your soul that Jehovah is God himself in the heavens above, and in the earth below, and there is no other, Deuteronomy 4:39.* 

From these things we gather that there is one light that is **supernatural**—that is, in its sole and absolute essence, without any respect to created things, which is also **super-celestial**, meaning it is exalted beyond the limits of nature; and another light that is **natural**, which again, due to the variety of place, or the subtlety or thickness of the air, is distinguished into **celestial** and **elementary**. It is **celestial** insofar as that light placed its tabernacle in the center of heaven—namely, in the sun—from which, by its luminous power and life, it imparts itself to the stars and ethereal creatures, such as the daemons <note>In this context, these are not "demons" in the modern evil sense, but intermediary spirits or "daemons" assigned to execute the laws of fate.</note> ordained for the execution of fate. It is **elementary** insofar as it radically informs all things, both simple and composite, in this region of the world: for it is the Word, in which is the life of things. For *the incorruptible spirit of God is in every thing,* insofar as it *touches everywhere because of its purity, and since it is permanent in itself, it renews all things—that is, it makes them flourish, grow, and multiply, Wisdom 7.* Whence it is said, *heaven and earth shall pass away, but the word of God shall remain forever,* for the spirit of God is incorruptible, and consequently is subject to no corruption, whence it also exists into eternity.

### CHAPTER III.
#### Concerning Universal Water and its species, and that it is the passive matter of any mixture, whether perfectly or imperfectly mixed.

Just as the internal form of all things, both mixed and simple, is a certain uncreated light, or a certain incorruptible spirit, divinely implanted in them from creation—without whose presence they could not live, or indeed exist at all—so also that spirit is the garment or the nearest vehicle of this light, by which the invisible air (namely, the wind) is moved at the command of this God-like spirit dwelling in the center. Its remote covering, and the nearest one to the air that carries it, is **invisible water**, both thick and thin, from which the bodies of creatures are forged. Whence it follows that all things in the world were created primarily from water and through water, by the operation of that central spirit; but secondarily from heaven, as the internal and spiritual part, and earth, as the external and corporeal part, since these two are what fill and complete the vast cavity of the world. And this is confirmed by Saint Peter, in the passage many times cited by us in the preceding pages, who says: *That the heavens were before, and the earth consisting of water and through water by the word of God.* Whence it follows that those things which are forged immediately from heaven and earth mixed together are originally made from water and through water; not, however, from the waters alone, which are the passive parts in the composition, but by the mediation of the acting divine Word, without which (*witness John*) nothing was made, insofar as the life of the creature is in it. Or, as was said before, through the mediation of Wisdom, *which was the brightness of eternal light emanating from the mouth of the Most High, originally before any creature, which (by the testimony of the wise man) was standing by her father in his works,* or as the leader Moses would have it, *by the mediation of the spirit of the Lord, which was carried over the waters,* providing them with fiery vigor or life.

We see, therefore, that the waters first created from mundane creatures are everything that is called "heaven" and "earth," and consequently, it is certain that they fill the vast concavity of the world. Whence also, just as the heaven or air expanded everywhere in its spiritual nature is of an invisible consistency, so the thin earth is visible water, but the thick or dross—and the "dead head," as it were, of the whole—is the opaque earth itself, which is of a more moist substance like the mud of the earth and mire, as well as of a drier and harder substance. So also we think it would not be absurd to distinguish between visible and invisible waters: namely, into **celestial** and **terrestrial**. But indeed it is certain that the invisible waters preceded the visible ones in creation, both in time and in order, for in them the heaven was established before any land or sea appeared.

### CHAPTER II.
### On the general distinction of dark Meteors.

| Meteors in the macrocosm, dark and collected | { Aqueous : See M. |
| and animated by the winds, are twofold, namely: | { Earthy : See N. |

Since everything in the world proceeds from the marrow and source of the dark Chaos <note>In Hermetic and alchemical thought, Chaos is the primordial "First Matter" from which God extracted the elements.</note>, as if from a material and luminous emanation of the Creator—with the said formal origin informing that general matter—we do not think it absurd that we have made a vast distinction in this meteorological discourse of ours between dark meteors and luminous ones. Yet we have not imagined such "chimeras" <note>In this context, a chimera refers to a baseless or impossible fiction.</note> as dark meteors in which no portions of primary light exist; for without participation in formal light <note> "Formal light" refers to the spiritual essence or "form" that gives a thing its specific identity and life.</note>, meteors would be nothing and purely potential. Rather, we call them "dark" because in them the formal light is hidden, and the entire mixture appears opaque and not at all luminous by itself to our eyes. 

Thus also by the testimony of the Holy Bible it is said, *Darkness was upon the face of the abyss*, Genesis 1. And yet *Wisdom walked in the depths of the abyss*, as we have in Ecclesiasticus: Eccl. 24. For darkness, according to the royal Psalmist, is not darkness to God, Psalm 139: and as elsewhere, *Thick clouds are a hiding place for GOD, who walks upon the circuit of the heavens*, Job 22. <note>original: "Densa nubes sunt latibulum DEI, qui ambitum cælorum obambulat."</note> And elsewhere, *The thick cloud is the vehicle or chariot of GOD, who moves upon the wings of the wind*, Psalm 104. Indeed, God himself said that *he dwells in darkness or under a thick cloud*, 2 Chronicles 6:1. And elsewhere, *He made darkness his secret place, and with the blackest waters and thick clouds he surrounded his tabernacle, so that they might serve him as a veil*, Psalm 18:11. Was it not also said that the darkness in Egypt arising from divine power was so great that one could not see another? and yet like a dark mist they were palpable <note>Exodus 10:21 describes a darkness that "may be felt."</note>, Exodus 10. And these are the dark meteors, aqueous or moist in condition.

Furthermore, the earth itself is accepted as darkness, and is called dark, as can be seen in many places of Holy Scripture; and consequently, we have not ineptly or rashly called all compact and opaque meteors—those of a terrestrial consistency—"dark." Such things include the Ceraunian stone <term>Ceraunian stone: Literally "thunder-stone." In early science, these were often prehistoric stone tools or fossils believed to have fallen from the sky during lightning strikes.</term>, manna, metallic bodies, and other things of this sort.

By a clearly similar reasoning, meteors in the Microcosm <note>The "Microcosm" is the human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note> are to be called either opaque or fiery. For as we see in the great world that the earth is as it were the source and origin of darkness—whence it is said, *The dark places of the earth are full of cruelty and violence* [Psalm 74:20]—so also it is said of the earth or human body: *The body subject to corruption weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling depresses the mind full of many cares*, Wisdom 9:15. #### First part: Concerning the dark aqueous meteors in the Macrocosm.

Dark meteors of an aqueous consistency are substances that are either thinner or thicker. We call those meteors "thinner" which are more spread out, softer, and less compact in their parts; these are halfway, as it were, in their movement from simple and invisible air to water as it is commonly understood. We call "thick" or "gross" those which are either liquid water or frozen, or which are compacted with earth, concerning which we will speak below. Aqueous meteors of a thinner consistency are various degrees of vapors or fumes, one of which is denser or heavier than the other, or closer to the water toward which they tend. Such types are the Halo, the Mist, and the Cloud, which we shall discuss here in more detail, first by explaining Aristotle's opinion on the origin or generation of such meteors, and afterwards how that opinion either agrees or disagrees with the testimony of Holy Scripture.

Aristotle, along with the rest of the Peripatetics, <note>The Peripatetics were followers of Aristotle, named for his habit of walking while teaching.</note> defines the **Halo** as a whitish circle with black around the edges, appearing around the Sun or the Moon or a bright star. It is formed from a moist vapor rising from the earth and waters, condensed into a very thin little cloud or mist, which creates a circular shape in the eyes of the onlookers beneath the celestial body. This is usually a sign of rain if it gradually turns black and becomes thicker throughout; but if it breaks with a huge crack on one side, it portends winds from that region where it first opens and bursts asunder. These are their views. Pliny also acknowledges that the circle of the Halo is sometimes of a blood-red color, due to the density of the cloud surrounding the sun (Pliny, Book 2, Chapter 30).

**Mist** <note>original: "Nebula"</note>, according to the opinion of the Peripatetics, is a kind of "sterile" cloud—that is, without rain—which remains from the residue of vapor gushing from the earth and waters that could not be raised high enough or condensed into a cloud. Or it may be defined thus: Mist is vapor drawn upward from the waters and earth by the heat of the sun; but because the solar heat is not strong enough to lift that vapor into the middle region of the air to be contracted into a cloud by the cold of that place, it allows it, after a small amount of condensation, to descend gradually back to the earth.

A **Cloud** <note>original: "Nubes"</note> (which is the most general category for the others mentioned) is vapor raised from the lands and waters into the middle region of the air by the force of solar heat, and there contracted and, as it were, congealed into the consistency of a cloud by the power of the extreme cold; afterwards, it is driven here and there through the middle region of the air, partly by the heat of the sun and partly by the force of the winds.

Finally, they define a **Little Cloud** <note>original: "Nubecula"</note> as a tiny cloud contracted by the union or addition of a vast magnitude of vapors flying upward in succession; hence the common proverb: *A great storm can often arise from a small cloud.*

In conclusion, therefore, all these meteors seem to differ not only in their material cause but also in their external form, insofar as some are more or less compact than others, and some are smaller or thinner in quantity than others. Therefore, once the matter and form of one have been investigated with diligent intuition, the others will reveal themselves more clearly by its light, since they are all of the same nature and condition.

In the definition of the condition of any meteor of this kind, three things are worthy of observation: namely, the **matter**, the **place**, and the **efficient cause**.

Aristotle makes the matter of the halo, the mist, and the cloud the same: namely, a moist vapor gushing from the earth and water, which are the places appropriate for its generation. But let us hear what the Holy Page <note>A traditional way to refer to the Bible.</note> relates concerning the origin of such little clouds and clouds, so that we may see by the testimony of the whole truth...

...created <note>The text begins mid-sentence: "[Spiri]tus creatum," referring to the "created spirit" of the air discussed on the previous page.</note>, so the eternal light emanating from God, and proceeding as if from His mouth, is an uncreated act, informing that created or passive spirit. This is also confirmed by the testimony of the Holy Scripture: *By His spirit He garnished the heavens* <note>original: "Spiritu suo caelos... ornavit"</note> (that is, the entire air), *Job 26:13.* This spirit is the central light, dwelling in inaccessible light, whence it is written, *God is clothed with light as with a garment.* <note>Psalm 104:2.</note> This light, appearing at times with its "garment," is seen in lightning and the sun, which is why it is sometimes called a *consuming fire*, the *fire of God*, etc. This, therefore, is that hidden spirit which does all things in the heavens and on the earth; in whose power it is (as stated before) to open the heavens—His greatest treasury—at His pleasure; that is, to bring forth from His treasury chest the mists, the clouds, and all other <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, rainbows, and clouds, not just falling stars.</note>. Whence it is also said elsewhere, *He opened the doors of heaven and rained down manna, Psalm 78:23-24.* <note>The original text cites Psalm 78:25.</note> We conclude, therefore, that air is the primary matter of the Halo as well as other meteors (of which more will be said in the description of mist and clouds); but Wisdom is the primary efficient cause, and her ministers <note>The winds.</note> are the secondary, or rather, the instrumental causes, as will be discussed more fully below.

Regarding the consistency of the Halo, it takes the form of a transparent mist—that is, a vaporous substance through which stellar rays can most easily penetrate. This consistency is applied in a denser or thinner measure according to the will of Divine Wisdom, in whose power it is *to give weight to the air, and to weigh the waters*—or vapors—*by measure, Job 28:25.* Thus it happens that, according to the diversity of quantity in density and thinness, He is accustomed to produce various effects according to the will of the Creator, as will be more clearly explained in our treatise on the final cause. It is necessary, therefore, that the consistency of this kind of meteor be not entirely of the natural constitution of air—inasmuch as air is invisible and consequently cannot visibly receive such impressions—nor of a dense mist or cloud, because a stellar body <note>A planet or star.</note> could scarcely, if at all, be seen through such bodies, and consequently could not imprint its coronal image upon it. Rather, it is a medium between corporeal darkness and that incorporeal state in which air is rendered invisible; it does not so obscure the light with darkness that it is not transparent, yet surely this transparency must not be without some shadow, because otherwise the reflection of an image cannot occur. Consequently, there would be no visible impression of the rays or the received image, just as can be seen clearly in glass and in the air itself. Hence <term>Algazel</term> <note>Al-Ghazali (c. 1058–1111), a Persian theologian and philosopher.</note> rightly says in *On the Nature of the Mirror*: *That no part of the celestial sphere is an object for the visual power, or receptive and retentive of the sun's light, except its denser part, which we call the star itself; because,* he says, *that sphere in its other parts, since it is more rarefied, is not bright when light is cast toward it, since it is not subject to color, and indeed is not visible.* This also <term>Haten</term> <note>Alhazen (Ibn al-Haytham, c. 965–1040), the "father of modern optics."</note> in Book 1 of *On Optics* <note>original: "de aspectibus"</note> seems to confirm, saying that what has no color is not visible, because (he says) a visible thing is not seen except according to the light in the thing seen; for visible light occupies only that which is colored. From this it is clear that the substance of the Halo must be misty, with a consistency midway between invisible spirit and an entirely opaque body, so that it may better receive the forms of the stars into itself. Whence <term>Albertus</term> <note>Albert the Great (c. 1200–1280), a medieval polymath.</note> says that the images of bodies can be most easily expressed in humid air, no differently than in a mirror or its reflections. From this it is also handed down that it happened to a certain person, on account of the weakness of his sight, that the nearby air in humid weather served him as a mirror, inasmuch as the rays could not perfectly penetrate through it but were partially reflected. The same thing is also accustomed to happen to those afflicted with most ruinous and dangerous illnesses and pestilential fevers; looking at their own faces in the air because of the weakness and poverty of their visual faculty, they believe they are staring at demons and foul forms, struck with fear. But I shall now proceed to the description of Mist.

### CHAPTER V.

*On the Description of Mist.*

**Mist** is a transmutation of the air from its natural and invisible consistency into a visible and thick vaporous substance, by the light of Wisdom acting centrally—that is, from within, contracting the air toward itself from all sides—and by her windy ministers from without, lightly compressing it with opposing blasts.
Or thus:
**Mist** is the primary species of dark visible meteors, created and brought forth from the first degree of air contracted into vapor, by the Divine will operating centrally and circumferentially.
Or thus:
**Mist** is a vaporous dwelling-place of God-like Wisdom, fashioned and contracted from the air by the magnetic attraction of the Lord dwelling centrally within it, and by the external compression of His winds.
Mist is therefore made of the same matter as its body, and of the same form as that of the Halo; the only difference lies in thinness and density—that is, in the formula of its composition.

Regarding the matter of this subject, although we have spoken quite abundantly in the preceding sections, something still remains to be explained in this place that was not fully demonstrated before. We have said, therefore, that the air is the immediate origin of the first stage of <term>meteors</term><note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, such as rain, clouds, or wind, rather than just space rocks.</note>—namely, vapor—which, by thickening more and more, is reduced into the consistency of a cloud. This invisible spirit is that from which all visible things were made, according to that verse so often cited before: *Through faith we understand that the world was framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear; Hebrews 11:3.* <note>original: "per fidem semper ita actum est cum mundo per verbum, vt ex iis quæ videri non poterant, fierent ea quæ possunt videri"</note> It is as if he were saying: from "nothing"—that is, from an imperceptible spirit—something, or a thing subject to the senses, was created. Thus the world was created from nothing, and likewise its creatures were produced from an equal "nothingness" (at least regarding our meager capacity for understanding), to be commemorated by faith alone. Through the power of the mediating Word or the Spirit of Wisdom, which shone forth before all things, this matter is brought into actual existence for us. Does not St. Paul also seem to acknowledge this same thing in these words: *God has chosen the ignoble things of this world, and those held as nothing, and those things which are not, to abolish those which are, so that no flesh should glory in his presence; 1 Corinthians 1:28-29.* <note>The author uses "1 Corint. 28. 29" as a shorthand for Chapter 1, verses 28-29.</note> By this he seems to argue that things of no apparent value or existence are, through the mediation of Wisdom, the cause of both the existence and the abolition of those things that do exist. For all generation and regeneration, and all corruption and resurrection from corruption, come from that invisible source through the mediation of that Christ, who is called by the Apostle *the power of GOD and the wisdom of GOD;* whence it follows in the next verse, *Christ Jesus was made unto us wisdom from GOD, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption; 1 Corinthians 1:23-30.* <note>The text cites verse 23, but the quote spans several verses in Chapter 1.</note> For this reason, the Apostle says elsewhere, *From him, in him, and through him are all things; to him be praise and honor, verse 36.* <note>Referencing Romans 11:36.</note>

But this same point is excellently expressed by the mystical Doctors and <term>Cabalists</term><note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance Christian philosophers.</note>. For Rabbi Bahir <note>A reference to the *Sefer Ha-Bahir*, one of the earliest works of Kabbalah.</note> says, *That there is no beginning except Wisdom;* which, being contracted in darkness or invisibly within the invisible spirit (according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus, *The Monad generates a monad and reflected its heat back into itself* <note>original: "Monas generat monadem & in seipsam reflexit ardorem"</note>—that is, it shone back upon itself), remained as if idle and devoid of action. That is to say, it had regard for "nothing," and in such a state it is called by the Hebrews *Ein* <note>original: "אין Ein"</note>, which means "Nothing," or "Non-being," or "Without End." So sterile is our apprehension, and so meager and powerless is our capacity for contemplating divine objects, that we judge those things which do not appear as if they did not exist at all.

But in truth, when it appears in reality in some form or substance, then the Cabalists say that *the dark Aleph is converted into the shining Aleph.* <note>Aleph (א) is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often used as a symbol for God's unity.</note> And just as *Aleph* is held by them to be the hieroglyphic for God—signifying unity and simplicity—so also by that "dark Aleph" they understand the Hidden GOD, and by the "shining Aleph," the Manifest GOD. To the truly Christian philosopher, this spirit—viewed in a general sense and endowed with the power of Wisdom—is defined as an infinite nature. It procreates like from like, generating and increasing all things, and contains the "names" <note>In this philosophical tradition, "names" refers to the essential archetypes or blueprints of things, rather than just their labels.</note> of all things within itself. For by its nature, it is animal, stone, wood, and tree; indeed, all visible bodies, whether they are <term>imperfectly or perfectly mixed</term> <note>In Aristotelian and alchemical thought, "perfectly mixed" substances are stable and enduring (like metals), while "imperfectly mixed" substances are fleeting or transitional (like clouds, snow, or rainbows).</note>, are animated by this spirit through divine wisdom and are held stable by its bond. 

It is the ligament of the elements and the power of mixing. By means of its "central soul" within every object in this world, it brings about the blending of the elements and imprints the form appropriate to its species, through which that thing is distinguished and separated from any other. Yet, this hidden nature possesses no specific color of its own, even though it shares in and creates all colors. It has no weight or quality itself, yet it is the source of all weights and qualities, and the fertile mother of all things. 

This is why Anaximenes boldly asserted that air is the cause of all things, and Anaximander regarded it as God, seeing it as the first [principle] of all things... <note>original: "vtpote primo rerum omn..." The sentence is truncated at the bottom of the page.</note>
