But that young man, wishing to show himself well-versed in the knowledge of <term>Peripatetic philosophy</term> <note>The philosophy of Aristotle and his followers, which sought purely physical explanations for natural phenomena.</note>, consulted with them and persisted in boldly persuading them not to fear. He affirmed that the phenomenon was common in nature and occurred by an accidental habit, and that there was no danger in it. He asserted that it was produced solely from a hot and dry exhalation from the womb of the earth, sublimated into the middle region of the air by the power of the sun's rays; he claimed the flame was procreated through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>original: "antiperiſtaſin." A philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat becoming more violent when trapped by cold air.</note>, which he said existed between the coldness of the place and the heat of the received exhalation. But it happened differently to him alone among the others than he had thought; for he was suddenly struck dead by lightning, while the rest, struck only with stupor and fear, fell to the ground. In this way, the blasphemy of that man—deceived by Aristotelian arguments—was judged by the righteous judgment of God.

In the year 1623, near the town they call Croydon, situated only eight miles from the city of London, around the month of July, certain people were preparing hay in the field of a certain nobleman. As they were drying it in the sun, they noticed voices and thunder approaching with horrendous lightning. Consequently, they divided themselves into two groups or pairs, huddling together no more than two cubits apart from one another, so that they might remain safer from the rage of the storm. Under one tree sat three young women with a certain boy; under another sat two or three men. As the storm approached (marvellous to say!), the thunder could do nothing against those under the first tree while one of the aforementioned maids remained under it, as if she alone had been marked on her forehead by God so that no evil spirit might bring her harm. Therefore, incited by an instinct of I know not what spirit, while the thunder and very heavy rain were falling, she proposed to leave that tree and hasten to the other. Addressing the others, she said, "I will hurry to the other tree; do you wish to come away with me?" But when the others refused, and she had taken five or six steps, immediately the other two women and the boy who remained under that tree—unwilling to leave with her—were struck by lightning and killed. No other sign appeared upon them except for a small scraping of the bark; however, the maid who left escaped safely to the men sheltering under the other tree. 

But what seemed an even greater miracle was this: fire in the form of a globe, descending from the top of that tree all the way to its root, rolled upon the earth like a wheel. It passed near the other tree under which the maid stood with the men; by its presence and passage, those standing there were not only alienated and astonished by stupor and fear, but the tree itself, moved by a certain remarkable reverence, was seen to bow toward that wheel and humble itself in such a way that the back of a robust man, who was leaning against its trunk, seemed to him to be broken by the great inclination of the tree. From this it is clear that there is a greater mystery in lightning and thunder than the Peripatetics could ever comprehend. Therefore, true Christians ought to apply themselves to the sense of the Holy Scriptures rather than to the vain and scarcely probable imagination of the Heathen Peripatetics, since the certainty of the former and the vanity and absurdity of the latter has been clearly declared in the preceding pages.

Furthermore, another wonderful example of this stupendous meteor in nature presented itself in the last year past, 1624, in the month of July, near the town of Windsor, where one may see the royal and well-fortified palace or castle, only eighteen miles distant from the city of London. For as two women with three girls were gathering ears of wheat scattered everywhere through the field after the harvest, a stupendous thunder suddenly came upon them. The eldest of the girls, seeing the lightnings flying everywhere through the air and appearing before her eyes in an oblong form with sharp tails, was greatly moved and disturbed in spirit beyond all the others. She cried out to her mother, "Fie on this lightning and thunder! I cannot endure it; I wish I were home!" And although she was admonished by her mother and another honest woman—who, before her marriage, was a servant or maid in my own house—that she should leave off such frivolous and contentious talk and call upon God, she nonetheless neglected prayers to God and continued her exclamations against the loathsome appearances of the meteor. Consequently, the others attempted to protect themselves from the violence of the storm under the "wings" or branches of two tall trees. But that girl, with a joking and cheerful face, leaning her back against the trunk of a very high oak, said that she was placed as if on a royal throne above the others and was secure from the storm. The other woman, formerly my servant, had her arm resting in the lap of said girl, and the girl's younger sister was not far from them, while the girl's mother stood under another tree five or six paces away. 

It happened then suddenly that a certain fiery globe falling from a cloud onto that huge tree stripped its bark in three places from the top to the root with a most violent and sudden force, without any interruption of the parts, and scattered fragments of it everywhere for nearly a mile's distance. Meanwhile, even the substance of the trunk and the internal body was not immune from that triple wound; but to the depth of a finger, hollow wounds were inflicted from the highest branches down to the root, as if by plowshares—doubtless the working finger of God or of some administering angel. Thus it happened that the girl, who thought herself most safe and protected from all violence, was suddenly killed in the blink of an eye by a force beyond words. The woman who was once my servant was deprived of the use and feeling of the arm that had been resting in the girl's lap, and she ran through the street or road in a frenzied manner, crying out with a loud voice and looking up at the clouds: "Holy God, open Your clouds and Your gates, that I may enter!" nor...

->**Correlation to the Microcosm**<-

We have learned from the teachings of both the more learned Theosophers <term>Theosopher: A "divine philosopher" who seeks knowledge of God through nature and mystical insight, rather than just rational logic.</term> and Philosophers that four things in the world were procreated according to the likeness of the Archetype <term>Archetype: The original divine blueprint or "Idea" in the mind of God from which all things were patterned.</term> and the primary Idea. Two of these were created via the natural path by the best and greatest Creator—namely, the World and Man—while the others were fabricated by the craftsmanship of a human creature, specifically the Ark or Tabernacle of the Covenant built by Moses, and that distinguished Temple built by Solomon. Just as those natural things were created according to the image of the Archetype, so too were the artificial things fabricated according to the pattern of the natural ones.

For in the World we have three regions, one of which excels the other in dignity: namely, the supreme region, which is the most excellent essence of all, called the **Empyrean** because of its fiery nature; and truly, just as fire is the element more eminent in dignity than all the others, and purer and simpler in essence, so for that same reason the Empyrean heaven is the head and Prince over the other two lower ones. For this reason, it is assigned as the seat for the purest and simplest of all creatures—namely, the Angels and the Intelligences who flash with divine splendor.

Then follows the middle region, which participates in both extremes and is called the **Ether** <note>In this system, the Ether is the celestial realm containing the stars and planets, sitting between the pure light of the angels and the heavy matter of Earth.</note>, because it seems to be composed of the supreme fire and the lowest air; for this reason, it is not quite as pure as that supreme region, nor so impure, thick, and unclean as the lowest, but consists in a middle state. 

Finally, the lowest region is thicker in quantity than the higher ones, more imperfect in quality, and subject to all changes: namely, the agitation of winds, the procreation of clouds, the crying out of thunders, and the ignition of lightnings, fiery whirlwinds, and other glowing meteors; to the soaking of rains, the flooding of waters, the insane and raging violence of winds bursting forth from the earth, the power of storms, and infinite other accidents occurring outside the laws of placid nature.

Furthermore, in Man—who was fabricated in the image of the world (whence he is called the "Son of the World" by Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercur. Trismegisto." Hermes Trismegistus is the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many foundational texts of alchemy and Hermetic philosophy are attributed.</note>)—we have an intellectual heaven assigned to the divine mind and its angelic sparks, which is his head, the seat of the **Holy of Holies**. In the middle region, or the celestial spirit, is the seat of life and the living soul; while the thick air of this human temple—namely the body—is the external seat, subject to so many and such great changes and the effects of "meteors" <note>In early modern science, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, as well as bodily "vapors" that caused disease.</note> tending toward both generation and corruption, so that it ought most aptly to be compared to the lowest region of the world.

Moses indeed confirmed this same thing in his method of constructing the Tabernacle, as did Solomon in his Temple. For their first part is uncovered and left open to the common air, subject to winds, rains, hail, snow, and other atmospheric impressions which are observed to form beneath the circle of the Moon; finally, it is subject to all alterations and changes. Therefore, common men of every kind approach this part, along with animals, where there is a constant cycle of life and death by reason of the continuous sacrifices. Hence it follows that this part is appropriately applied to the arrangement of the elementary world, seeing as it is composed of water as a fluid and unstable substance; thus the world is truly called a place of shadows and obscurity. For this reason, the Tempter is sometimes called the Prince of Darkness, sometimes the Prince of the World, and sometimes the Prince having the power of the air.

The second part of the Tabernacle or Temple is covered and shines inwardly with gold; it is illuminated by a candlestick with seven branches, which without doubt denote as many planets. Hence this region of the Tabernacle undoubtedly represents the celestial world in the Macrocosm, participating in both light and darkness—namely, fire and thin water. For this reason, the heavens were called *Eschamaim* <note>original: "Eschamaim." A transliteration of the Hebrew word for heavens, *Shamayim*.</note> by the Hebrews, from *Esh* (fire) and *Maim* (water). From this it is clear that the substance of the heaven is truly a body, but incorruptible, imbued with a certain intellect by which it is governed and to which it is annexed, so that this matter is neither free nor wandering. The rational soul in Man, or the Microcosm, has such a relationship to his body.

The third part of the Tabernacle or Temple was the **Holy of Holies**, presenting the figure or image of the intellectual world. This is the seat and domicile of the fiery angels and the abstract or "separated" intelligences (who are the ministers of the living God). This is also signified within it because two golden Cherubim, with wings extended wide, cover and overshadow the Mercy Seat. Furthermore, we have all these regions in the human temple, differing in every way by purity and impurity. Thus it happens that, just as in the Great World we receive all influences from GOD through the most pure and fiery world into that which lies immediately beneath it—namely, by means of the *Sephirot* <term>Sephirot: In Jewish Kabbalah, these are the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself and creates the universe.</term> through the angelic or empyrean region into the ethereal—so likewise does that ethereal region influence the sublunary, called the elementary region...

...already mentioned, in which so many and such great transformations occur in the world; in the same way, within the human world, the mental force acts through the intellect to exert its influence upon the ethereal region—where the force of life resides. Ultimately, by these influences, the aerial spirit <term>Aerial spirit: In Renaissance medicine, this was a subtle substance that circulated through the body and nerves, acting as a bridge between the physical soul and the material body.</term>, dispersed everywhere through the body and the blood vessels, is ruled and governed for the fulfillment and preservation of human life. Indeed, we possess the essences of these internal regions from those of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World" or the universe at large, which was believed to be perfectly mirrored by the "Microcosm" or the human being.</term>. Beyond that double breath—namely, the common one which the Creator assigned to the world for its completion, and that specific one which He Himself breathed into the face of Adam as the "breath of life"—it is necessary that the small parts of every macrocosmic region attributed to man in his creation should converge toward the perfection of the regions of the Microcosm.

Furthermore, by the same logic, it is clear that the lowest region of the Macrocosm (the air), when burdened and disturbed by the presence of various "meteors" <term>Meteors: In this historical context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, lightning, and clouds, not just falling space rocks.</term>, also communicates constantly with the human air. For the air that is commonly inhaled and breathed in through the nostrils, the windpipe, and the pores of the Microcosm, joins with the air enclosed within the human. Through this communication, the human spirit becomes a participant in and possessor of the natures and impressions previously generated in the "Great Air," which are then scattered through it and enclosed as if in seed-beds. 

And just as in the Macrocosm, God rains down influences through His "shining gates" into the angelic world—procreating all meteors, whether favorable or malevolent—and that world passes them to the celestial world, which finally sows them everywhere through the elemental world: in this same way, God is the general actor in all these things. His act is the effect of His Word, dispersed everywhere, whether as Wisdom, or as a shining emanation and emission. Therefore, it is also manifest that all diseases procreated in man proceed from God in no different a manner than those meteors in the Great World. Just as the outflows of the Divine Will descend first through various orders of angels according to a varied logic of emanations—who then pour them into the stellar bodies of the ether, from which they are finally rained into the lower realms for the procreation of meteors and impressions of every kind—so too the winds, acting as spirits and angelic impressions (both occult and manifest), are the ministers of God. They act first in the open air, so that they may then act in various ways and paths upon the human air to execute the will or pleasure of God, whether for good or for evil. 

Hence, as was said regarding the Great World, *at the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire; and the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice, and coals of fire; he sent out his arrows and scattered them; he multiplied lightnings and troubled them, etc. Psalm 17:49.* <note>original: "Ps. 17:49." This corresponds to Psalm 18 in modern translations.</note> In this passage, the "arrows" can be understood as the rays of lightning, which is why it is said elsewhere: *The shafts of lightning shall go directly, and as from a well-curved bow of clouds they shall be driven out, and leap to a certain place. Wisdom 5:22.* In the Microcosm, God acts in such a way by means of the Microcosmic spirit; namely, by igniting a fire in its aerial spirit no differently than He does in the macrocosmic air.

Therefore, Job breaks out in these words: *The arrows of the Almighty are heavy in me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit; and the terrors of God, set in array, fight against me. Job 6:4.* And elsewhere: *Jehovah shall make the pestilence cleave to you until you are consumed; Jehovah shall strike you with a burning wasting disease.* This happens in the wrath of Jehovah, of which it is spoken: *The wrath of Jehovah becomes like a consuming fire.* And elsewhere: *God shall consume the wicked with fire.* And regarding this in another place: *Pour out your heat upon other nations.* Furthermore, the leprosy falling upon Miriam can be compared to snow. But regarding these matters, we shall speak most abundantly in our *Preternatural History of the Microcosm*. Now, however, we shall descend with a light leap to the description of the angelic ministers of God, whose task it is to fulfill the commands and pleasures of God.

### **Chapter II.**
### *On the Essence and composition of the Angel: what is its external, and what is its internal?*

A great dispute and discrepancy has arisen among the most skilled philosophers and theologians regarding the "angelic consistency." Some (among whom I name Damascene, Thomas Aquinas, and Dionysius) affirm that an Angel is something absolutely incorporeal. However, Basil, Origen, Gregory, and Hermes Trismegistus, along with the entire School of the Academics <note>The "Academics" here refers to the Platonic and Neoplatonic philosophers.</note>, wish the angel to be a corporeal substance. Augustine, in his commentary on Genesis, says in express words that "demons are animals of air and fire," and consequently he seems to assign airy bodies to them. Indeed, elsewhere he does not hesitate to assert that angels, from the beginning of their creation, had airy bodies formed from the purer part of the upper air—suited for acting, but not for suffering <note>In this context, "suffering" (patiendum) means being acted upon or changed by external physical forces.</note>. He argues that the evil angels were changed by their fall, their bodies taking on the quality of thicker air, so that they might be capable of suffering and being tormented by fire. Basil teaches us what kind of bodies were assigned to angels by God at creation: namely, that they are thin, airy, and pure spirits. Artesius <note>Likely referring to Artephius, a medieval alchemical author.</note>, in his *Key of Wisdom*, says that the "external" of the Devil is air, but his "internal" is fire; for this reason, he teaches that it is very easy for the Devil, by means of his external part, to join with the "airy spirit" within a human being, and in this way produce burning diseases.

As for our own opinion, it is most certain and proven by clear reason that Basil, Gregory, Origen, and all the Academics do not stray from the truth when they say that daemons or angels are "incorporated" from air in their external aspect. Hence, according to the varying thickness or thinness of the air, different orders of daemons are found in the world, differing from one another in nature and condition. For just as it is observed in the order of nature that "subtle air" is nothing but pure fire, and "medium air" is nothing but wind, and "thick air" passes into the nature of water (the density of which eventually becomes earth itself), so for that very same reason, some daemons are fiery, others airy, others watery, and some earthy. Consequently, in respect to their external part, all are "airy"—that is, subtly corporeal insofar as they are made of air.

For who, having even a slight acquaintance with philosophy, can be ignorant of the fact that rain-water was first a dense cloud, and that the dense cloud was previously derived from a type of misty vapor? That misty vapor which is visible to the eyes was once an invisible vapor, which is the first step in the progression from medium, invisible air to that which is thick and visible. This alteration happens through degrees of thickness. Therefore, reason compels us to accept this regarding the varied constitution of angels; and from this arises the mystery of angelic mutation from one species to another, from a visible form to an invisible one, and vice versa. It is certain, then, that insofar as angels are airy, they are to that extent corporeal. For unless air in its invisible nature were corporeal, it would be impossible for it to be condensed into a visible body. That which produces a result must possess that quality in its origin; air, by its positioning, produces clouds, water, and earth through the path of condensation. Therefore, it undoubtedly possesses a corporeal nature within itself, otherwise it would be impossible for it to be altered into the appearance of a body. This, then, was the reason why some daemons are fiery—namely, those who are clothed in the thinnest and rarest air.

In this figure, therefore, is clearly explained that proportion by which any order of angels abounds both in matter and in form, and also by what proportion the divine emanation immerses itself into the multitude—that is, into the depth of the formal pyramid. In the contemplation of this image, you will also see with open eyes how all things have proceeded from **God**, and how they shall return to **God**, according to that saying of the Apostle: *And consequently how one is all, and all at last are nothing but one.* <note>original: "iuxta illud Apostoli: Et consequenter quomodo vnum sit omnia, & omnia tandem non sint nisi vnum." A reference to the Neoplatonic cycle of "proodos" (procession) and "epistrophe" (return), framed by St. Paul's theology in Romans 11:36.</note> Furthermore, in the proper speculation of the formal pyramid, you will perceive what the Kabbalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism who explored the nature of the divine through the Sephirot and the Hebrew alphabet.</note> understood by their great angel **Metatron** <note>original: "Metattron"; a high-ranking archangel in Jewish mysticism often considered the mediator between God and the universe.</note> or the emanation from **Ehyeh** <note>original: "Ebieh"; Fludd's rendering of the Hebrew divine name "I Am," representing the highest source of emanation.</note>—which is that **Wisdom** so often cited in the scriptures—and what the Platonists meant by the **World Soul**, and the poets by **Pan** and **Panthea**. You will see how an angel is "otherness," namely from the created pyramid—which is material in respect to its exterior—and the uncreated or formal pyramid in respect to its interior; hence angels are called mirrors that receive divine lights. Finally, you will see what created nature is—namely, the material pyramid which is made from primordial water—and what that uncreated nature is—namely, the informing pyramid. This informing pyramid is nothing other than the emanation or flowing forth of divinity into the spirit or worldly water, which was once overwhelmed by darkness and formless, but is now informed by the divine presence—that is, brought into the light. In conclusion, we can perceive that creation is nothing else than the mingling of the divine emanation with that which is to be recreated; without this, it could not persist for even a moment. Hence it is said that *all things were made by the Word, and without it, nothing was made that was made.* <note>A direct reference to the prologue of the Gospel of John (John 1:3).</note> Hence we say that God fills everything and is everywhere; hence the Apostle said, *In God we move, and in Him, through Him, and from Him all things exist,* etc. <note>A combination of Acts 17:28 and Romans 11:36.</note> Truly, the **Angels** are called creatures of the first composition, because their matter, being the thinnest of all, was the first to receive the effects of the creating emanation, which is therefore called by the wise the "first of all creations."

But lest you misunderstand me when I mention pyramids—since the word "pyramid" seems to sound mathematical, and moreover I have described them in a mathematical fashion with a base and a cone—I wish you to understand that I am speaking of a **physical pyramid**, and not a mathematical one. I have been forced to describe the former by means of the latter because it is more commonly known. By a physical pyramid, I mean the **worldly spirit**, which, ascending from the earth to the periphery of the world, always gradually renders itself thinner and more subtle in its ascent, until it reaches the extreme perfection of rarity at its apex—beyond which limit matter cannot ascend. But that which is beyond the capacity of matter must necessarily belong to the divine essence. Does not experience itself seem to declare this same thing? For all coincide in this—the physicists as well as those more skilled in theology—that water is subtler than earth, air than water, fire than air, ether than fire, and the **Empyrean spirit** than ether. This spirit also has its own degrees up to the cone of the physical pyramid. Here, therefore, we have expressed the material pyramid both physically and mathematically, so that what has been said by us may be more easily conceived by you.

...can a visible body be produced by the addition of parts? Therefore, whatever can be understood within the laws of rarity and density can be called (and not without justice) a body. In the same way, since a cloud is a dense form of air, why should the rare form of air not also receive the name of "body," since that which is easily made into such a thing is itself of that nature? What then? Because it is a natural body, is it therefore not also a spiritual body? The Apostle says: *The body that is sown in corruption rises in incorruption; the natural body will be changed into a spiritual body.* <note>original: "Corpus quod seminatur in corruptione surgit in incorruptione, corpus naturale mutatum erit in spiritale Corpus." This is a reference to 1 Corinthians 15:42-44.</note> It is therefore no more impossible for a sublunary spirit, or an ethereal one, or even the empyrean or angelic spirit to be a "rare body"—and consequently for angelic creatures to be made corporeal by their presence—than it was for that corporeal body of our Savior, which was made incorruptible after his passion and raised and sublimated by its purity and subtlety all the way to the throne of GOD. In that covenant, he is said to sit at the right hand of the Father, and yet he nonetheless did not lose the name of a body. Wherefore, we should not be faulted for assigning an external corporeal nature to angels of any order, because all matter—whether it be subject to corruption or of a celestial and incorruptible nature—is contained within the limits of corporeal substance. For who can rightly deny that water reduced to vapor is a body, just as much as it is in the form of liquid water? Or that the tip of a material pyramid is less of a body than its base? The whole difference lies in rarity and density; but truly, because something is a dense body, a rare body is not thereby excluded. Therefore, I hope it has been explained clearer than light that angels, as far as their external aspect is concerned, are corporeal and not incorporeal, as some have thought.

As for their internal aspect, we say it is uncreated light. Thus, the exterior of angels is like a highly polished, very bright, and stainless mirror, receiving within itself the ineffable likeness of God. For in it, as if in a clean and pure mirror, the divine splendor shines back, emanating immediately from the divine majesty. Whence (as was declared in the preceding pages) angels are called *Agalmata* <note>A Greek term for "cult images" or "statues," used here by Fludd to mean "most clear mirrors" reflecting the divine.</note>, that is, most clear mirrors receiving the light of GOD. For this reason, an angel is said to be the image of God, the revelation of hidden light, a most polished and pure mirror without a stain.
*Dionysius, On the Divine Names, chapter 6.* <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite was a key source for Christian angelology and the idea of celestial hierarchies.</note>

For they receive through influence the light of the Deity, which in itself is incomprehensible and invisible, and they show it, emit it, and reveal it to others of an inferior order. The angel is called a "mirror" because it is capable of receiving light, and it is called a "most polished mirror" because of the complete purity of its substance. Another says that angels are "intellectual lights" receiving light from the First Light. Moreover, that descending emanation—which flows into the bodies of angels as well as into other creatures through their mediation—is what the Kabbalists call *Hochma* <note>original: "Hochma Sapientia." Hebrew for "Wisdom," the second Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</note>, namely Wisdom. This is why the wise man calls it the "first creature," since it proceeds immediately like a son from a father, from a bright fountain. Solomon describes this as a holy spirit of intelligence, more mobile than all mobile things, reaching everywhere because of its purity. He says that in its essence it is a vapor of the power of God, and a certain pure emanation or flow of the brightness of the almighty GOD, and the whiteness or splendor of eternal light, and a mirror without stain of the majesty of GOD, and an image of His goodness. *Wisdom of Solomon 7.* <note>Fludd is quoting the apocryphal Book of Wisdom, identifying the Holy Spirit/Wisdom with the substance of angels.</note> Hence, according to the doctrine of the Kabbalists, this spirit is that great angel **Metatron**, whose role is to animate the entire universe, and whom the Platonists were often calling the "Soul of the World." For this reason, it is also said that the Name of GOD is in the angel—that is, the Divine light or the Word that gives life to all things and is the first mover in the angelic composition. Whence angels are ministers through whom, as if through instruments, the word of GOD is perfected in this world. Therefore, the Psalmist says: *Angels of GOD, most mighty in strength, doing his word, listening to the voice of his word, his ministers doing his pleasure.* *Psalm 103.* And elsewhere: *Behold, I send my angel before you; listen to his voice, because my name is in him.* *Exodus 23.*

We conclude, therefore, that an angel is composed of a **created spirit** (which is its external part and serves as its body) and **uncreated light** (shining immediately from GOD, which is its internal part and by which it is animated). By means of this composition, an angel is sometimes called "Angel" or "Otherness" in the Holy Scriptures with respect to the composition of its whole (being made of two things, namely internal and external). Yet in another place, the angel is called **IEHOVAH** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God.</note> with respect to its internal part alone, which is the emanation of GOD. Thus, it is sometimes said that an "angel" was in the burning bush, and sometimes that "Jehovah" spoke to Moses from the bush. For this very reason, the Name of GOD (the syllable "El") is assigned to the angels of GOD, as in Gabri-**el**, Micha-**el**, Rapha-**el**, etc. <note>The suffix "-el" means "God" in Hebrew; Fludd argues these names prove that God's essence dwells within the angelic form.</note>

...are of importance on Earth to care for things, seeing as they are accustomed to be present for individuals, and indeed to care for every creature, whether animal, vegetable, or mineral. From these things, it is clearly established that each of these hierarchies has a special relationship to a person in the Most Holy Trinity: the highest hierarchy relates to the divine essence <note>The Father</note>; the middle to the emanation or the Son, as it regards the monarchy and governance of the heavens; and the lowest has respect for sublunary <note>earthly</note> things, as it is present in the forms and virtues of lower things and is seen to administer them.

It is in this sense that the royal Psalmist appears to speak in very few words, saying: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their power by the spirit of his mouth* <note>original: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt cæli, & spiritu ab ore eius omnes virtutes eorum"; Psalm 33:6. Where the Lord, or the Father, created the heavens by the Word, or the Son, and every virtue and influence by the Spirit [proceeding] from both, etc.

According to the division of the ancient Hebrews, we see these same orders of angels—the same in both number and effect, though varying in their names—following the series of the "Bright Gates" or <term>Sephirot<gloss>the ten attributes or emanations in Cabala through which the Infinite reveals itself</gloss></term>, or the "Numerations" of the Cabalists, through which the various influxes of divine properties descend to the lower things. For as we have declared elsewhere, the influxes of *Kether* <note>The "Crown," the first Sephirah</note>, over which the name of God *Ehieh* presides, descend through the order of the **Seraphim** according to the doctrine of <term>Dionysius<gloss>Dionysius the Areopagite, a 5th-century Christian mystic who wrote the definitive guide to angelic hierarchies</gloss></term>. Thus, according to the sense of the ancient Hebrew Doctors, God *Ehieh* is said to bestow the gift of being through the order of angels called the *Haioth Kadosch* <note>original: "Haioth Kadosch"; Hebrew for "Holy Living Creatures"</note>; through the *Ophanim* <note>Wheels</note>, God distinguishes the Chaos; through the *Aralim* <note>Mighty Ones</note>, Jehovah is said to provide the forms of universal matter; and so it continues for the rest, as will be made clearer in what follows. The Hebrew Doctors have given other names to these angelic orders, nearly the same but with the order changed: namely, *Chasmalim*, *Cherubim*, *Tarshishim*, *Aralim*, *Seraphim*, *Malachim*, *Ophanim*, *Issim*, and *Elohim*. To these they also enjoy adding the *Bene Elohim* <note>Sons of God</note>, by which they mean spirits both good and evil (of which more below). And they have fished out all these names from the holy source of the sacred pages themselves. For Ezekiel speaks of the *Chasmalim* <note>Ezekiel 1:4; often translated as "glowing metal" or "amber"</note>. Genesis, Exodus, and the Psalms mention the **Cherubim**. Ezekiel also names the *Tarshishim* <note>Ezekiel 10:9; often translated as "beryl" or "precious stones"</note>, though common interpretation offers "angels" or "messengers" in its place. Ezekiel also has the name *Ophanim*; as the *Issim* <note>Souls of the Just</note> are expressed by Solomon; and they had *Elohim* from the first book of Kings, where the <term>Pythoness<gloss>The Witch of Endor, a spirit medium</gloss></term> said to Saul: *I saw Elohim ascending from the earth* <note>1 Samuel 28:13</note>, that is, "gods" or "divine beings" according to the common edition. Mention of the good *Bene Elohim* was made by Job, and of the evil ones by Moses and also by Job in another place.

However, it is not irrelevant to note that although only nine orders of angels are noted by the wise or the more secret Theologians, there is nevertheless an innumerable multitude of individuals within each of those species, which they have named "armies." They divided each of these orders, primarily according to the partition of the celestial Zodiac, into twelve parts; the first member in this division they called *Mizaloth* <note>likely a variant of "Mazzaroth," the Hebrew term for the Zodiac constellations</note>. Then, they divided each of these twelve members into thirty portions, which they called **Cohorts**. Consequently, each contains thirty cohorts for each of those twelve, which makes a total of three hundred and sixty cohorts of Angels.

Afterward, they assign another subdivision which multiplies those 360 by 30, producing the number 10,800; this subdivided member they call a **Legion**. They multiply this number again by 30, and they produce what they call a *Ribaton*, consisting of 324,000. Furthermore, they multiply this number by 30, and the resulting number they call a *Chitton*, which is composed of 9,720,000 <note>The Latin text says 972,000, which appears to be a calculation error in the original manuscript's sequence</note>. Finally, they lead that product again by 30, and the resulting number will be 29,160,000. Whence the sum of all these, according to the doctrine of the Cabalists, is one million, six hundred fifty-five thousand, one hundred and seventy-two <note>1,655,172</note>. They made all these angels "ministering spirits," about which more will be said in the following pages. The Platonists, however, maintain that there are as many legions of lower spirits as there are stars in the heaven, and they say there are as many spirits in each legion as there are stars in the heaven. And some of the Cabalists strenuously defend the idea that angels agree with humans not only in many natural things but also in number, asserting that there must be as many humans to be saved as there were rebel angels who fell from heaven in the conflict and battle between Michael and Lucifer; and again, that there will be as many damned as there were angels on Michael's side who obtained victory over the fallen angels.

But whatever the opinion of the Cabalists and Platonists regarding the number of angels may be, we also gather from the sacred letters that there are many myriads of angelic spirits. This is found in several places: *The chariots of God,* says David, *are two myriads, many thousands of angels; the Lord is among them, the Lord of Sinai, dwelling in the Sanctuary* <note>Psalm 68:17-18</note>. Furthermore, Christ speaks of many legions of both His Father and of Satan. And Augustine and Gregory maintain that the number of good angels transcends all human grasp; to which, in contrast, correspond innumerable unclean spirits, there being as many in the lower world as there are world-spirits in the higher world. Certain Theologians have also confessed to having received this from oracles. Celestial spirits are called "worldly" by the more Secret Theologians <note>This likely refers to students of the Christian Cabala or Hermeticism.</note>. Furthermore, those who dwell in the firmament and its stars are called Olympics; their duty is to decree the fates and to administer fatal events to lower things, according to the will and permission of God. Hence it happens that neither an evil spirit nor an evil fate can harm one who "dwells in the aid of the Most High" <note>A reference to Psalm 91:1.</note>.

Moreover, it is decreed for each of these spirits to carry out that which the star to which it is attached portends. Nevertheless, without divine permission, it can bring nothing from potentiality into action; for God alone is the one who grants them the power and the execution. To Him, as the creator of all things, it is given that the supercelestial, the celestial, the sublunary <note>earthly</note>, and even indeed the infernal realms must obey and submit.

As for the spirits presiding over the fixed stars, those who hold their kingdoms in the Zodiac preside either over the triplicities—namely of fire, air, water, or earth—or over individual whole signs. Specifically: *Malchidael* over Aries, *Asmodel* over Taurus, *Ambriel* over Gemini, *Muriel* over Cancer, *Verchiel* over Leo, *Hamaliel* over Virgo, *Zuriel* over Libra, *Zarachiel* over Scorpio, *Advachiel* over Sagittarius, *Hanael* over Capricorn, *Cambiel* over Aquarius, and *Barchiel* over Pisces.

But truly, the names of the angels of any sign are usually derived from the harmony they have with the name of the sign they preside over. Thus, from Aries comes Ariel; then Telechiel, Suriel, Tommiel, Sartamiel, Betuliel, Mafniel, Acrabiel, Chefitiel, Gediel, Deliel, Dagymiel. It is as if we were to say in Latin letters: Ariel, Tauriel, Geminiel, Cancriel, Leoniel, Virginiel, Libriel, Scorpiel, Sagittariel, Capriel, Aquariel, Pisciel. 

In any case, it is certain that each of these signs has its own peculiar governor or angel. The Cabalists believe that John understood this in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> when, in the description of the Celestial Jerusalem, he mentions the 12 gates of the city. By these 12 gates, he means the 12 celestial signs, which Plato calls the "gates of heaven." In each of these gates, the Apocalypse says an angel is present, for it assigns 12 angels in express words to the 12 gates of the heavenly city. And just as there are three Eastern signs, three Western, three Southern, and finally three Northern signs according to the doctrine of the Astrologers, so the revelator <note>St. John</note> recognizes and assigns three gates to the eastern quarter, the same number to the western, three to the south, and the same number to the North.

Furthermore, the Cabalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah) whose ideas were heavily integrated into Renaissance occult philosophy.</note> assign an inferior angel to all the decans <note>original: "decuriis"; these are ten-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign.</note> of the signs, which the Astrologers call "faces," and even to the quinaries <note>Five-degree subdivisions of a sign.</note>, which are half-parts of a face. According to their opinion, every angelic triplicity <note>A grouping of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> also rejoices in its own angelic prefect.

Abbot Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot and polymath famous for his works on cryptography and steganography, which often used angelic names as a "cover" for codes.</note>, in a particular treatise dedicated to Emperor Maximilian, testifies that every planetary sphere has a prince spirit or intelligence, through whose mediation the world is successively governed. Through these spirits, all things that exist in heaven and air, and those that live and grow on earth, are by the will of the Creator fatedly disposed. The Prince or superior prefect destined for the governance of Saturn is called *Zaphkiel* by the Magi (as some would have it); others call him *Oriphiel*. After him follows *Zadkiel*, or *Zachariel*, who presides over Jupiter; then *Zamael* or *Samael* (or *Camael* as others prefer) over Mars; *Michael* over the Sun, although some make *Raphael* its prefect; *Haniel* or *Anael* over Venus; *Raphael* over Mercury, though some attribute *Michael* to it; and *Gabriel* over the Moon. 

Regarding these spirits reigning over the planets, John seems to understand them in Apocalypse 1 <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> when he says, *“And from the seven spirits who are in the presence of the throne of GOD, etc.”* Raphael also understood this when he said to Tobit, *“I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand before Jehovah.”* <note>original: "Iehouam"</note> And Gabriel said to Mary: *“I am Gabriel, who stands before God” (Luke 1).* And elsewhere he says to Daniel: *“Behold, Michael, one of the princes, came to my aid” (Daniel 10:13).* *Zachariel* was also the good angel of the Prophet Zechariah, of whom he writes: *“The angel who spoke in me went out, and said to another angel, 'Run...' etc.” (Zechariah 2).* 

These princes or prefects have many cohorts of inferior spirits under each of their commands. These spirits, according to the mandates of God, are constantly flowed into lower things by way of influence to carry out the will of their president. This occurs more abundantly according to the dominance of the star in heaven which they are said to inhabit. These inferior angels or spirits <note>original: "dæmones." Used here in the classical sense of intermediary beings, not necessarily evil demons.</note> receive their general names from their star. Just as we say "Frenchman," "Englishman," "Spaniard," or "Italian," we understand a man born in France, England, Spain, or Italy; so also by reason of their nature we call the inhabitants of those spheres Jovials, Saturnines, Martials, and so forth.

The angels under the command of the Great Archangel Gabriel, however, are accustomed to vary in nature and disposition according to the various positions of the lunar sphere within the signs of the Zodiac, which the Astrologers call "mansions." These mansions are 28 in total, and therefore the angels governing them are called by various names, which we list in order as follows: *Geniel, Enediel, Amixiel, Azariel, Gabriel, Dirachiel, Seheliel, Amnediel, Barbiel, Ardestel, Neciel, Abdizuel, Iazeriel, Ergediel, Ataliel, Azeruel, Adriel, Egibiel, Amutiel, Kyriel, Bethnael, Celiel, Requiel, Abrinael, Aziel, Tagriel, Alheniel, Amnixiel.* All of these have great power both in the various changes of water and air, and in the alterations of terrestrial things.

Finally, according to the doctrine of the Cabalists, there are other angels to whom the four watches of the night are committed, of whom Christ speaks thus: *“And if he shall come in the second or third watch of the night, etc.”* Others are set over the four watches of the year, according to those four stations of the sun which occur in Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn <note>The Spring Equinox, Summer Solstice, Autumn Equinox, and Winter Solstice.</note>, etc.

### CHAPTER IV.
### On the diversity of wicked and malignant Demons.

Just as God, who is the Emperor of light, is the Emperor of goodness, so also the Devil, who is the great Prince of darkness, is the author and operator of evil. From this it follows that as God uses good angels for his ministers (who are therefore called angels of light), so conversely the Devil has many troops of Demons under his command, divided into legions. To these it is given to invade and harm the aerial spirit of both the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World," or the universe at large.</note> and the Microcosm <note>The "Small World," referring to Man as a reflection of the universe.</note> in a malignant manner. Relying on these matters, confirmed by the authority of many trustworthy writers, I shall proceed to distinguish the multitude of Cacodemons <note>From the Greek *kakodaimon*, meaning an evil spirit or malevolent entity.</note> in this manner:

Evil spirits are malignantly engaged either concerning:
*   Spirit alone:
    *   Of the Macrocosm (A)
    *   Of the Microcosm (B)
*   Spirit and body together:
    *   Of the Macrocosm alone (C)
    *   Of the Microcosm alone (D)
    *   Of both together (E)

The entire composition of both the world and man consists of spirit and body. But indeed, since the universal spirit of both worlds is divided into three regions (as has been declared by us many times before): First, the Empyrean heaven, which is the seat of the good angels, from which the malignant angels—on account of their ambitious rebellion—were relegated as if into exile to the dense and lower region of the universal spirit. To this upper region of the mundane spirit corresponds the intellectual or rational spirit in man, which is the angelic seat of the mind. Next, in the world, there is the middle seat of this universal spirit, which is called the ether, in which the Olympic Angels or Demons <note>Spirits associated with the stars and planets; in Renaissance magic, they were often viewed as neutral or administrative forces governing the cosmos.</note> act. These are called the distributors of Fate because they rain down both malevolent and benevolent influences (according to the pleasure of the supreme creator) into the region of the elements; it is from these that the sublunary demons, both good and bad, receive their powers in action and their dominations. 

From this it is clear that Satan, who is the Prince of the Air, can do nothing without permission and varied influx, according to the varied disposition of any Sephirotic numeration <note>A reference to the Sephirot, the ten attributes or "shining gates" in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life through which divine energy flows.</note> or "shining gate." To this middle region of the spirit of the world corresponds the vital spirit in man, which sometimes inclines toward higher things and sometimes toward lower and fleeting things. Finally, the spirit of the sublunary world <note>The region below the moon, consisting of the four elements: fire, air, water, and earth.</note> is that which (by divine permission) the great Prince of darkness commands. To this corresponds the natural spirit in man, which Paul seems to call the "animal soul" <note>original: "animam animalem." This refers to the lower, sensory soul driven by biological instincts rather than spiritual reason.</note>, whose appetite is occupied with the flesh and its pleasures. Hence the Prince of the Air is said to have power and to operate in the sons of disobedience, as will be clear below. What the orders of the Cacodemons in the elementary air are, and what their conditions are, may be gathered from the following members of the Cacodemonical division:

Cacodemons exercising their powers in the sublunary spirit of the world (namely, the air) differ in rank, as some are:
*   Principalities or Spirits of a higher order:
    *   Emperor.
    *   Kings (F).
    *   Dukes (G).
*   Subjects or those of an inferior condition, subjected to the aforesaid leaders, who are divided from one another into cohorts and legions (H).

Just as in the Empyrean Heaven one may find Principalities, Archangels, and Angels of a benign condition, so indeed Lucifer, once cast down from that throne with his angels, has similar ministers under him, distinct in order and rank. We have this confirmed even by the Apostle, whose authority is this: *“Put on,” he says, “the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the snares of the devil, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against Princes and powers, against the world-rulers of these darknesses, against spiritual wickedness in high places,” etc. (Ephesians 6:12).* <note>original Latin quote: "Induite armaturam Dei...". The author is citing the Vulgate translation of the Bible.</note> By these words he clearly teaches that the Devil, as if the supreme king and emperor of wickedness and malignancy, has ministers under him eminent in condition, whom the Apostle calls Princes and powers of darkness, world-rulers, and spiritual wickedness. Hence also in another place the said Apostle says, *“You walked according to the age of this world...”*

It is from this, therefore, that according to the twelve prefects of the celestial signs, our Savior makes mention of legions of angels, saying: *Do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father, and he will at once send me more than twelve legions of angels? Matthew 26:53.* <note>original: "An putas, quod non possim rogare patrem meum...".</note> Regarding these twelve prefects of the signs, and the masters of the four triplicities, which are related to the gates of the heavenly city—namely, three in the East, and as many in the West, as well as in the South and the North, along with the angels who are their guardians—we have spoken before. By a similar reasoning, the wicked angels are also ordered into legions; hence when Christ asked of the Demon, *What is your name? he answered, my name is Legion, for we are many: Mark 8.* <note>The author cites Mark 8, though the "Legion" encounter is usually found in Mark 5:9.</note> By this we can note that the substance of a Demon is very minute, like a solar atom, and consequently that there is an infinite multitude of demons flying everywhere in the air. This is also confirmed by the express words of the Hebrew Doctors, whose opinion is that from the earth all the way to the firmament there is no empty place, but everything is full of forms—some of them pure, others capable of grace—and below there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images, dwelling and flying in the air. Similarly, in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis", referring to the *Sha'are Orah*, a primary text of Jewish Kabbalah by Joseph Gikatilla.</note> it is held that there is no empty place from the earth to the firmament, but that the whole is filled with species: some for war, some for peace; some for good, some for evil; some for life, and some for death; and all of this is in the inferior habitation in which we exist, as reported by Joseph Castaliensis. From these things it is evident that the number of demons, both bad and good, in this elementary region in which we breathe, is infinite to us. Some of these are from the region of the East, others of a southern nature, some western, and others northern with respect to the quarter of the world, and also the triplicity whose temperament and condition they share.

I also posit that from the nature of the planet by whose influences they are chiefly animated and quickened, some are called Saturnine, others Jovial <note>associated with Jupiter</note>, Martial <note>associated with Mars</note>, Solar, Venereal <note>associated with Venus</note>, Mercurial, and Lunar. These are the subjects of the Angels or Intelligences presiding over the Planets. Thus it happens that when Saturn is predominant in the horoscope or celestial scheme, because of his copious inflows at that time, the spirits in the elements sharing in his nature tend to predominate, and so it is with the others.

Finally, each of these is called by a general name based on the element in which it naturally participates, and in which it commonly and most willingly lives as if in its own fatherland; and in this many who are most well-versed in the mysteries of demons agree. For first, the Kabbalists and Hebrew Doctors say that the squalid and most foul demons are enemies to the human race, whence in their opposition to the good angels they are called Angels of contrary strength. But they confess that some of these wander through the highest region of the air, whom they therefore call **fiery**; those who are accustomed to wander closer to us they call **aerial**; those who terrify terrestrial things they name **terrestrial**; just as those who inhabit lakes and rivers and often shake the sea they name **aqueous**; and finally, those whom they call "light-shunners" <term>lucifugos<note>From the Latin 'lux' (light) and 'fugere' (to flee); spirits that avoid the light.</note></term> and dark, they place **underground**. Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher and author of 'De Operatione Daemonum' (On the Operation of Demons).</note> also seems to confirm this from the confession of Marcus, saying that only six kinds of these demons are found in the elementary region.

Of which:
1. The first is **fiery**, which is seen to wander about the sublime region of the air.
2. The second is **aerial**, which wanders near to us.
3. The third is **aquatic**, which immerses itself in humors, namely lakes, ponds, rivers, and the sea.
4. The fourth is **terrestrial**, which for the most part is occupied around the earth.
5. The fifth is **subterranean**, which is accustomed to dwell under the earth.
6. The sixth and last is **light-shunning**, inscrutable, and dark.

These kinds of "Cacodaemons" <term>cacodaemon<note>A Greek-derived term for an "evil spirit" or "malevolent entity."</note></term> are said to hold God, Angels, and even men in hatred; of whose properties and conditions we shall soon speak more at length.

**On the evil Demons hovering around the human spirit.**

Evil spirits <note>original: "Cacodæmones"</note> who hover around the human spirit are distinguished into six <note>The text initially says six, but then lists eight; this reflects a common numbering discrepancy in Renaissance manuscripts or a transition between different systems of classification.</note> degrees, of which:
The First infects with Idolatry and vain or false worship, and entices one toward the adoration of itself.
The Second contaminates with lies and deceives with false whisperings, and leads into error.
The Third inflates with anger and fury, and finds various arts to kindle passions within them.
The Fourth fills with vengeance, retribution, and cruelty.
The Fifth deludes with illusions and false miracles.
The Sixth ignites with the heat of discord, wars, and devastations.
The Seventh brings charges, spies upon, and accuses before the sight of God.
The Eighth casts one into error and danger through temptations and snares, and stains with despair.

The first degree of evil spirits, which infests the human spirit with Idolatry, is the order of those who are called "pseudothei," that is, false gods <term>pseudothei<note>From the Greek 'pseudos' (false) and 'theos' (god). In Renaissance demonology, these were spirits who masqueraded as divine beings to steal the worship intended for the Creator.</note></term>. For it is the nature of these to falsely attribute the name of God to themselves, and to lure the human spirit toward their own cult and adoration through false and deceptive demonstrations. Their prince is thought to be Beelzebub, which means the "Ancient God," <note>original: "vetustus Deus". While Beelzebub is traditionally translated from Hebrew as "Lord of the Flies," the author here interprets it as "Ancient God."</note> who is so bold that he did not hesitate to tempt the spirit of the Savior of the world himself by saying: *All these things I will give to you, if you will fall down and worship me.* Matthew 4. To this degree also belonged the Gods of the Midianites, who, through the daughters of Moab (with whom the people of Israel committed fornication), seduced those people from the worship of the true God, and persuaded them to adore them and to immolate sacrifices or burnt offerings. Numbers 25. Such also was the spirit of the Oracles, namely of the Delphic Apollo, etc.

The second degree comprises those who are accustomed to introduce and whisper falsehoods into the spirits of men. Of this order was that lying spirit which, by divine command, entered into the mouths of the Prophets of Ahab: 1 Kings 22. Similarly, it is the spirit that strikes terror and dread into the spirits of men, of which it is written: *Behold, I will send a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land.* 2 Kings 19. Furthermore, the prince of this order is called by those skilled in magic "Python," that is, the serpent.

The third degree consists of those who set the human spirit ablaze with the love of iniquity and the flames of anger and fury. To perform this duty more easily, they invent games, such as cards, dice, and other things of this sort, by which they stir men toward passion and wrath. Such a demon was the one named Theuth, whom Plato says was the master of games, specifically of dice. The Hebrews establish the prince of these to be Belial, which is interpreted as "without a yoke," "disobedient," or "transgressor," etc.

The fourth degree or order is that which not only drives the human spirit toward vengeance and retribution but has itself become the author of Divine vengeance. The royal Psalmist seems to show a precaution against the invasions of this kind of Demon into the human spirit with this discourse: *Refrain from anger, and forsake burning wrath, lest you be incensed even to do evil; for evildoers shall be cut off.* Psalm 37:8. And the wise man says: *Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.* Ecclesiastes 7. And elsewhere: *Make no friendship with an angry man, and with a furious man you shall not go.* Proverbs 22:24. Furthermore, that he is the avenger and the minister of God's vengeance is indicated by this passage cited from Holy Scripture, where such a demon is called: *The spirit of the power of God, winnowing and pursuing the unjust with justice.* Wisdom 11:21. And of him elsewhere: *The spirit of power and the spirit of virtue shall stand against them.* Wisdom 5:24. The Cabalists and Mages identify the prince of these as Asmodeus, which means "the one who executes justice." <note>original: "facientem iustitiam". Asmodeus is more commonly associated with lust in other traditions, but here he is linked to the destructive aspect of judgment.</note>

The fifth degree is of those who delude with illusions and false miracles. The magicians of the Egyptians required the assistance of these when, attempting to act against Moses, they produced so many deceptive miracles in the presence of Pharaoh. Cacomagi <term>Cacomagi<note>From Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'magos' (magician). These are practitioners of "black magic" who work with evil spirits for harmful ends.</note></term> and sorcerers implore the help of such as these in their business. Finally, the mages themselves affirm the Prince of these to be Satan, of whom it is said in the Apocalypse that he deceives the whole world, performing great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men, so that he may seduce those dwelling upon it.

The sixth degree is said to disseminate discord, war, devastation, and unbridled desire through the human spirit; the Prince of these is called **Apollyon** <note>original: "Apollyon"</note> in the Apocalypse and **Abaddon** <note>original: "Abaddon"</note> by the Hebrews, which translates to "the exterminator" or "the destroyer." Of this same order was that Angel standing between heaven and earth, whom Jehovah sent to destroy and lay waste to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21:15). It also includes the one who killed every man of great strength in the camps of the King of Assyria (2 Chronicles 32).

The seventh degree is accustomed to bringing charges, spying upon, and accusing spirits before the sight of Jehovah. The mages call this spirit **Astaroth**, which means "the explorer" <note>Astaroth is often depicted in Renaissance grimoires as a high-ranking duke of hell; here, the author focuses on the role of a celestial spy or prosecutor.</note>, and in Greek, he is called **Diabolus** <note>original: "Diabolum," from the Greek 'diabolos,' meaning an accuser or slanderer.</note>, that is, the accuser and slanderer.

The last degree attempts to deceive the human spirit with temptations and snares, leading it into error and desperation. The Prince of such demons is said to be **Mammon**, whom they interpret as personified **Greed** <note>original: "Cupiditatem." In biblical contexts, Mammon represents wealth or material gain pursued as a false god.</note>.

230 [centered] **Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.**

Now, the lowest region of the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the entire universe, viewed as a living organism mirroring the human "Microcosm."</note>, in order to be subject to various passions and changes, is observed to have its airy spirit distinguished into various degrees of corporeity <note>The state of having a physical body or substance.</note>. This occurs before both the external body and its internal spirit are afflicted and agitated at any given degree by the angelic ministers of God—namely, by those who are like winds and those who are like burning flames. For David confessed that *God makes his angels winds, and his ministers a burning fire: Psalm 104:4.* <note>original: "Deus faciat angelos suos ventos, & ministros suos ignem vrentem"</note> And in the preceding psalm: *That the angels of God, most mighty in strength, carry out the word of God, listen to the voice of his command, and that they are the armies and ministers of God doing his pleasure, etc. Psalm 103:20.* <note>original: "Quod angeli Dei validissimi robore efficiant verbum Dei, auscultent voci eius, & quod sint exercitus & ministri Dei facientes placitum eius"</note> In this speech of the royal Psalmist, we are taught that there are three principal orders of angels: the first and superior order, receiving the emanations of God directly, is accustomed to "carry out"—that is, to receive and send forth—the word of God; the second order listens to and notices that word, as if issued by the Supreme Emperor, and then commits that mandate to the legion assigned to its dominion for execution; the third order is that which immediately performs and executes the pleasure of the Creator.

The more recent theologians also seem to admit this same point. Namely, that the superior orders of angels receive light or emanation directly from God, which they afterwards impart and communicate to the lower orders by flowing into them.

Moreover, God uses certain of these angels to execute the effects of his wrath and vengeance; these we call "evil spirits" <note>original: "malignos"</note> and "cacodemons" <note>original: "cacodæmones," from the Greek for 'evil spirits.'</note> in respect to ourselves, yet they are nonetheless necessary ministers of God. Thus, God used Satan as his minister to tempt Job. So also was that destroying Angel of Jehovah, whom David saw with eyes lifted up, standing between heaven and earth with his sword drawn in his hand and extended against Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21). And also that one whom Jehovah sent to cut down every man of great strength in the camps of the king of Assyria (2 Chronicles 32). Such also was that evil spirit of Jehovah which obsessed Saul, etc. He also uses certain angels in his kindness, who are called good and benevolent spirits. Such was the Angel who, appearing to Elijah in the desert, offered him food; and the one whom God sent before Moses and the Israelites to keep them on their journey through the desert (Exodus 33). And that Angel who claimed Jacob from all evil (Genesis 48). And the angels who met him on his journey (Genesis 32). Finally, all those angels whom God sends before the righteous (Genesis 24:7). Similarly, by the ministry of good angels, the spirit of the Macrocosm is governed kindly and peacefully, just as it is perturbed by the predominance of tumultuous spirits, at which time even sublunary bodies <note>Objects or beings existing below the moon, subject to change and decay in the four elements.</note> seem to fall ill.

The first "incorporation" <note>The process of taking on a physical or denser form.</note> that occurs between simple air and a perfectly mixed body is "vaporous" or "misty" air. In this air, various preternatural impressions are produced by evil spirits: namely, inflammation from the *prester* <note>original: "prestere." A classical term for a fiery whirlwind or a lightning strike accompanied by a violent storm.</note> and lightning, perturbation from winds and whirlwinds, gloom from mists and thick vapors, the evening redness, etc. Concerning the intemperance of the air caused by the *prester*, the Holy Scripture speaks thus: *Behold, a whirlwind came out of the North, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst of the fire as it were the appearance of amber, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of living creatures, and a spirit in four wheels, etc. Ezekiel 1.* <note>original: "Ecce ventus turbinis veniebat ab Aquilone... species electri"</note> By these things, the Prophet wishes to imply that the soul of both that cloud and that *prester* was that spirit, or rather the driver of that chariot; and the Lord who was carried in it was Jehovah himself, as we can gather from that entire chapter. And Isaiah says, *The Lord God of hosts shall visit it with thunder, and with shaking of the earth, and with a great noise of whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire. Isaiah 29:6.* And Jeremiah says: *Behold the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing tempest; it shall rest upon the head of the wicked. Jeremiah 30:23.* And the royal Psalmist: *He rains upon the wicked snares, fire, and brimstone, joined with a shifting whirlwind. Psalm 11:6.* And elsewhere: *As the fire burns the forest, and as the flame consumes the mountains, so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your whirlwind. Psalm 84:15.* And of the whirlwind, Isaiah says *it comes from the South. Isaiah 21:1.* And Zechariah: *The Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south. Zechariah 9:14.* And Job says: *Out of the inner chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds. Job 37:9.* That is, from the spirits or demons who, by their blasts, do the will of God from the North. We conclude, therefore, that its internal part is the stormy spirit of God, executing the word and will of God, as the Prophet David acknowledges. Whence also the wise man says: *The spirit of the power of God shall stand against the wicked, and like a whirlwind of wind shall scatter them. Wisdom 5.*

Furthermore, clouds are the vehicles of God which are carried and animated, and are seen to be moved in the air with violent motion and preternaturally perturbed by the angels of God and His presence. In His presence, the angelic ministers always stand and assist; hence the Prophet says: *He ascended upon the Cherubim, and flew upon the wings of the winds, and he made darkness his hiding place; round about him was his tabernacle, dark waters in the clouds of the air; at the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire. The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Highest gave his voice, hail and coals of fire; and he sent out his arrows, and multiplied lightnings, and troubled them, etc. Psalm 17:9.* <note>This corresponds to Psalm 18 in modern Bibles.</note> In this speech, the Prophet clearly teaches that the ministers of the Lord are the Cherubim and the winds, as if he had said: the angels listening to His voice, and the winds or angelic spirits, the fiery ministers, performing His pleasure, as he admits elsewhere. And elsewhere he says: *The waters saw you and were afraid, and the depths were troubled, the multitude of the sound of the waters gave a voice...*

It describes how both "good" and "evil" spirits influence the atmosphere of the Macrocosm to bring about either peace or divine judgment.</summary>
