<meta>This page continues the discussion of how angelic beings—both benevolent and malevolent—act as the intermediate causes of physical phenomena within the Macrocosm (the universe). It specifically addresses how God uses these ministers to manipulate the elements of water and earth, following the previous discussion of air and fire.</meta>

->On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 231<-

...your ministers a burning fire; the abyss like a garment is his covering; the waters shall stand upon the mountains; at your rebuke they shall flee; at the voice of your thunder they shall be afraid, Psalm 104:2. <note>original: "ministros tuos ignem vrentem, Abyssus sicut vestimentum amictus eius, super montes stabunt aquae, ab increpatione tua fugient, à voce tonitrui tui formidabunt"</note> By these words, it seems to be argued that Jehovah is the prince and supreme commander, who has his tabernacle in the clouds, whom angels—both fiery and windy—serve, and that the clouds seem to be disturbed, to fear, and to roar at the sight of his splendor, and finally to behave in a <term>preternatural</term> <note>Beyond the ordinary course of nature, but not necessarily miraculous; here referring to weather events driven by spiritual forces.</note> way. 

The third step in the progression from the invisible nature of the air to a perfectly mixed body is water, whose primary element is the sea. This sea, along with rivers and lakes, is either made peaceful by the good spirit of Jehovah or disturbed by the evil spirit of Jehovah, and is stirred up to the harm of sailors. Hence the royal Psalmist says: *You break the ships of the ocean with the East Wind,* Psalm 48:8. <note>original: "Oceani naues perfringis Euro"</note> That is, sent forth by a violent blast from <term>Samael</term> <note>In certain mystical traditions, Samael is an archangel associated with severity, judgement, or the "left hand" of God; here he is linked to the destructive power of the East Wind.</note> or the East by divine will. And elsewhere: *Who disturbs the depth of the sea,* Psalm 65. And elsewhere he acknowledges that the sea was stirred up by the rebuke of Jehovah, and that the sea, seeing Jehovah, fled, Psalm 114:3. And Job says: *By his power the sea is still, and by his understanding he struck down pride,* Job 26:12. <note>original: "Potentia eius quiescit mare, & intelligentia sua perculit elationem"</note> From this, one may see that it is God’s role both to disturb and to make quiet the sea, or the element of water.

But the royal prophet also expresses this perfectly and in most clear words elsewhere, saying: *Those going down to the sea in ships, they see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep; and he speaks, and makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow, and it lifts up its waves; they rise up even to heaven, they descend even to the abysses, so that their soul melts away in evils; they are tossed and reel like drunkards, so that all their wisdom is swallowed up. Then they cry out to Jehovah in their distress, and he leads them out of their troubles; he makes the whirlwind blow into silence, and their waves are still; they celebrate Jehovah’s mercy, and preach his wonders to the sons of men,* Psalm 107:23-31 <note>The text cites verse 33, but the passage corresponds to verses 23-31 of Psalm 107.</note>. Here, therefore, you see first that Jehovah is the commander of all powers, and the first mover and operator of all things; secondly, that in his severity he deals harshly with the elements of the world because of the sins of men; and then thirdly, that he acts through his angelic ministers, who are always ready—according to their own good or evil office—to carry out the commands and divine pleasure. For he says: *And he makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow.* 

But at the repentance and cries of men for mercy, he makes the tumultuous whirlwind stand still. Here, moreover, the spirit of the whirlwind is an angelic wind, executing God’s severity upon the sea. By the command of Jehovah, it acts within the internal spirit of the seas and lakes in an insane, tumultuous, and furious manner—no differently than that evil spirit of Jehovah acted in the internal airy spirit of Saul himself, or the demon called "Legion" in the possessed man, which was cast out by the power of Jesus and entered into the swine. Or as in those vexed by the worst epilepsy, who swell with a great swelling and cast foam from the mouth, or in those affected by that rabid disease called <term>Lycanthropy</term> <note>A delusion in which a person believes they have changed into a wolf; here the author uses it as an analogy for violent, irrational movement in nature.</note>, who are tossed and carried here and there in a violent manner. Thus does that violent spirit act with its legions in the sea, lakes, and ponds, etc.

Finally, since the earth is a thicker part of water, we have now come to it; and we say that it too is sometimes tossed and struck by the evil spirits of God. Hence Holy Scripture says: *The earth is shaken and moved, the foundations of the heavens are moved; it is shaken when anger is kindled against it,* 2 Samuel 22:8. <note>original: "Concutitur ac mouetur terra, fundamenta caelorum commouentur..."</note> And elsewhere: *God moves the earth from its place, so that its columns tremble; he transfers mountains,* Job 9:5-6. And elsewhere: *At God’s look the earth trembled, and at his touch the mountains smoke,* Psalm 104:32. But indeed, in such an act of God, he himself uses spiritual ministers destined for that work, who, by the command of the angelic prefect, shake the earth, produce huge chasms in it, vomit fires from its bowels, and are accustomed to perform many other terrible things on the earth. Hence also, when God was angry because of the impiety of the Jews, it was said: *Behold, a great earthquake occurred, for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning, etc.* Matthew 28:2. Sometimes also, through his avenging angels, Jehovah sends down fire and sulfur upon the earth, by which it is overturned and treated in a preternatural way. And Jehovah (says Genesis) sent down upon Sodom and Gomorrah a rain of sulfur and fire from the heavens, and overturned the city and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants, and the produce of the earth, etc. Genesis 19:24. But indeed, that Jehovah used his angels in such a business is explained in that very context. 

And elsewhere it is said: *The land is burned with salt and sulfur, so that it can neither be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow upon it, etc.* Deuteronomy 29:23. This Jehovah produced for the inhabitants of the earth through the mediation of his ministers because of their sins. And elsewhere: *Jehovah will make the rain of your land powder, or dust shall descend from the heavens upon you until you are destroyed,* Deuteronomy 28:24. Furthermore, in another place the Psalmist says: *He turns a fruitful land into saltiness, because of the malice of the men dwelling in it; conversely, he turns a desert into a pool of water and a parched land into springs of water, etc.* By which he seems to argue that in his severity, God makes the earth dry and sterile, or suffocated by an excessive flood of waters, because of the sins of men; which he himself is handed down to do through his ministers by the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of thought in Jewish mysticism; here Fludd refers to their complex systems of angelic hierarchies governing the physical world.</note> and those versed in the deeper mysteries of God.

For just as they assigned angelic prefects to the elements—namely, Seraph to fire, Cherub to air, Tharsis to <insert>water</insert> <note>The original Latin reads "Tharsis igni" (Tharsis to fire), but in the system Fludd is citing, Tharsis is almost always the angel of Water, while Seraph is Fire. This is likely a scribal or printing error.</note>, and Ariel to Earth, who are good leaders—so indeed under them four malevolent spirits act wickedly: namely, <term>Samael</term> from the fiery part, <term>Azazel</term> from the airy part, <term>Azael</term> from the watery part, and <term>Mahazael</term> from the earthly part. Under their command (as said before) are many orders of inferior demons. Therefore, both fiery and bright storms, along with such comets, proceed from the fiery angels; likewise, airy impressions come from the airy angels, as do those that disturb the waters from the watery ones. And it belongs to the earthly spirits—as <margin>Evil Spirit 7. i.</margin> <term>Psellus</term> <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078), a Byzantine scholar and philosopher whose work on the classification of demons was highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> testifies—to produce chasms in the earth, to shake the foundations, and to send upward flame-vomiting winds.

<summary>This page explains the "efficient cause" of weather and geological events, arguing that God uses specific hierarchies of good and evil angels to manipulate the elements—water and earth—as rewards or punishments for humanity. # On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 233

In this way, would he [an angel] bring a plague upon him? *1 Chronicles 21*. Yet, even when a man sins, it is not within the power of a destroying angel to afflict him with evil unless God—casting aside His mercy and donning the cloak of severity—says "Let it be done," or "I shall strike." Thus in Exodus, we have this pronouncement from God: *I will send all my plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants, and upon your people in all the earth, Exodus 9:14.* And elsewhere: *The Lord shall make the pestilence cling to you, and the Lord shall strike you with consumption, and with a burning fever, and with inflammation, and with extreme burning, and with drought, and with blasting, and with jaundice, which shall pursue you until you perish. And the Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with the scab, and with the itch, whereof you cannot be healed. And the Lord shall strike you with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart, so that you shall grope at noon-day as the blind gropes in darkness. And he shall strike you in the legs and in the knees with a sore botch that cannot be healed, Deuteronomy 28.* 

Once these things are pronounced by God, a "bad angel" stands ready as a "Let it be done," along with his subordinates, to carry out what God has spoken. Thus it is said that the devil struck Job with terrible boils, *from the sole of his foot even unto his crown, Job 2.* And yet Job, in this adversity, said: *the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit; the terrors of God are set in array against me, etc.* And elsewhere: *You lift me up to the wind; you cause me to melt away in substance: Job 30.* 

By these examples, one may see that where a destroying angel is permitted to afflict a man with disease, that entire work—though performed through a minister—is ascribed to God. He afflicts with disease through evil angels, just as, conversely, He restores health through good angels. 

For evil angels do not afflict with disease, nor do good ones bless a man with health, of their own accord; rather, both health and disease come from God through the angels. From this it follows: *If you will diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do that which is right in my eyes... I will put none of these diseases upon you which I brought upon the Egyptians, for I am the Lord your healer, etc.* <note>Exodus 15:26. The author emphasizes that God is the primary "Creator" or restorer of health.</note>

This means: "I will bring it to pass and command that the good angels—such as Raphael <note>The name Raphael means "God heals" in Hebrew.</note> and his host—shall care for you," or "My word [shall come] through an angel, etc." Hence the name Raphael is as if we said, "God healing."

We conclude, therefore, that it is God who strikes and who heals, but He does this through His ministers, the angels, whose role is to do His pleasure. Thus, no evil demon can strike without the permission of the good angels, nor can they grant permission or cease their guardianship (for everyone has their own good guardian angel) unless God commands it. 

Mention is made of these types of spirits, contrary in their condition, in the passage where it is said: *that the good spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. Wherefore his servants said: Behold now, an evil spirit of God troubles you, 1 Samuel 16:15.* Thus it is also manifest that evil angels, or <term>cacodemons</term> <note>From the Greek 'kakodaimon,' meaning an evil spirit or malevolent deity.</note>, are the instruments of God in His severity, just as the good are in His mercy. David confesses this in open speech: *He cast upon them the fierceness of His anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them; He struck every firstborn, and spared not their souls from death, etc. Psalm 78:49.* <note>The text cites Psalm 77, following an older numbering system.</note> 

From these passages it is clear enough that although Moses speaks of "the destroyer" or a destroying angel, there were many angels or cacodemons assisting in that work. Arresius <note>Likely a reference to a medieval medical or theological authority.</note> declares the aptitude of demons—by which they have power over men abandoned by God—in these words: "There are certain infirmities in which the devil joins himself to a humor exiting its proper temperament and disturbing health itself. This happens most especially in infirmities arising from <term>cholera</term> <note>Yellow bile, one of the four humors, associated with fire and heat.</note>. The reason is of this kind: because the internal nature of the Devil is fire, just as his external nature is air; hence he can easily be joined, God permitting, with the human air."

So says Arresius. But it is the role of the good angels to bind the elements in harmonious peace, as they are the "sons of concord." When these angels, by divine will, vacate their office, it happens that the evil demons—who are the "offspring of discord"—suddenly invade and attempt to turn human harmony into dissonance. From this it is clear that demons are accustomed to procreate any disease in the human body according to their respective elements.

Hence Albohali <note>An 8th-century Arab astrologer, Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat.</note> says that Melancholy comes from a demon. And Alzarabius <note>Abulcasis, a famous medieval physician.</note> says that sicknesses invade men through the transgressions and curses of demons, who are called the *Alhabinables*. And Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher and demonologist.</note>, from the revelation of Marcus, says that aerial spirits or demons bring harm to men by approaching the <term>phantastic spirit</term> <note>The part of the soul or 'vital spirit' responsible for imagination and sensory processing.</note> within us, due to the similarity of their natures. For in this way, words of disturbance and pleasure sound within us—not by emitting a voice through physical vibration and sound, but by projecting their speech without sound. They speak into the ear in a silent manner, like whispering. They present various colors to the imagination according to their will, insofar as they are "aerial," for air is capable of all colors. 

From this, the "phantastic essence" transmits figures, colors, and whatever forms they themselves wish into our animal spirit. Thus they cause us much trouble: suggesting desires and plans, representing forms, arousing memories of pleasures, and frequently stirring up the images of passions in those who are both awake and asleep. Sometimes by tickling our thighs and groins, they submit and sharpen insane and iniquitous loves; they disturb the soul with a certain art and sophisticated fraud. 

But truly, the watery and earthy demons devise nothing with wisdom, nor do they perform anything by craft, except that which is troublesome; they injure in the manner of a <term>Charonean spirit</term> <note>A reference to "Mephitic" or suffocating vapors associated with caves (Charonean vents), which were thought to kill instantly.</note>. It is the property of these spirits to corrupt whatever they approach, whether it be a four-footed beast, a man, or a bird.

It has been declared by us that a certain sage in "Secret Theography," in a certain treatise of his entitled *The Revelation of Majesty* (*Book on the Spirit*, chapter 78), breaks forth into these words: All things were created through the Word of God; therefore, all things are also governed, moved, and led through the Word. For this reason, the "wise men" or philosophers of the world are raving when they fail to concede that God works all things in all, and that His Word moves, stirs, and preserves everything. Instead, they ascribe these things to created nature, pretending that God works through "media"—namely, through secondary and tertiary causes. They are unwilling to understand that God works solely through His Word, and not through any other media or the aforementioned alleged causes, but only *within* them. 

The first body—namely water—God created as moist and liquid through His Word. Thus, there appears to be no other cause in water that makes it wet and liquid. Above and within the water, God created the "hidden air" so that it might float upon the waters, impel and move them, and preserve them in their liquid and flowing substance; this same thing happens even today. Along with the air, He also simultaneously created angels and spirits by His Word. These spirits perform their duty and office in the air regarding the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, and the "thunderstone" <note>original: *lapidis ceraunii*; historically, these were prehistoric stone tools or fossils believed to fall from the sky during lightning strikes</note>, fire, atmospheric chasms <note>original: *chasmatum*; referring to openings or "gaps" in the sky, often associated with auroras or meteor sightings</note>, floods of water, heat, cold, warmth, moisture, dryness, and many other things of this kind. So says that author. 

From these points, it is clear that God does not work "mediately" <note>meaning through a chain of independent tools</note> through the angels, but through the Word *within* the angels. This is also what Rabbi Menahem Recanati <note>a famous 13th-century Italian Cabalist</note> says in his commentaries on Exodus 14: "The characters flying above in the foundation of spiritual wisdom are the administrative spirits, used to perform every thing through them; and their operations are known to the Cabalists." <note>The "flying characters" refer to the Hebrew letters, which Cabalists believe are the spiritual blueprints of reality.</note> 

But lest anyone, led by vain superstition, should think that all things are conferred upon human mortality from heaven by the angels alone, we have therefore asserted with Reuchlin <note>Johann Reuchlin, a prominent Christian Cabalist</note> in Book 3 of *The Cabalistic Art*, that all things are done by the Majesty of God itself through the angels as if they were organs—even *within* the angels. This is also testified by the Prophet Daniel, speaking to King Nebuchadnezzar: *According to His will He does in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth.* For the Word of God has impressed its own "character" <note>a spiritual mark or seal</note> upon every angel. Hence, Jehovah says of the Angel whom He placed as a leader for Moses on the journey through the desert: *He will not bear your transgressions, for my name is in him.* 

And this is why the names of the angels end in *El* or *Iah*, such as Michael, Haziel, Hahaiah, Jehuiah, Habriah, etc. <note>*El* and *Iah* (Yah) are names of God in Hebrew; adding them to a name signifies the angel is an extension of Divine power.</note> From this it is clear that it is God within the angel who acts and incites the angelic creature to accomplish this or that according to His will, and not the angelic creature itself. However, insofar as the "whole angel" is considered—namely its internal and external aspects—it is said by those with a worldly sense (or the men of the world) that this or that is done *by* the angel. 

Therefore, it follows that an angel, whether good or evil, can do nothing against the divine will, but is moved where and when God (or the Word marked within him) pleases to lead him, so that he may execute his office in this or that place according to the Divine property that leads or carries him away.

Regarding the Star of the Christ, as the Magi intended when they said, *For we have seen His star* (Matthew 2), it was as if they had said it was led by His angel. This is similar to what was said of the pillar of fire in which the angel resided, whom Jehovah placed before the Israelites on their journey: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day, and a starry light by night* (Wisdom 10:17). 250 **Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Book IV. Member II.**

He is properly called **Beelzebub**, which means "Ancient God" <note>original Latin: "Vetustus DEVS." While Beelzebub is more commonly translated from Hebrew as "Lord of the Flies," the author here uses a different etymological tradition</note>; under his dominion are those demons called **False Gods**, who desire to be held and worshiped as gods. From this, they scatter the seeds of idolatry in the human spirit and by this path entice them to sin. Such was the one who tempted Christ to worship him. Another is named **Python**, that is, the serpent, under whom are the spirits and the lying legions: he seduced Adam and Eve with his lies away from obedience toward their creator, and with his false affections, he is accustomed to contaminate the children of Adam even to this day, so that they are rendered disobedient to God.

The third is **Belial**, which is interpreted as "without a yoke," <note>a traditional Hebrew etymology meaning "without worth" or "worthless," often rendered in Latin as *absque iugo*</note> the disobedient transgressor and apostate. The demons under his command are called "vessels of iniquity" by Jacob in the blessings of *Simeon and Levi, Genesis 49*. They are called "vessels of wrath" and "vessels of death" in *Psalm 7* by the royal Psalmist; "vessels of fury" by Isaiah in *Isaiah 13*; "vessels of wrath" by Jeremiah in *Jeremiah 50*; and "vessels of slaughter and destruction" by Ezekiel. Likewise, they are the inventors of the evil arts.

The fourth is **Asmodeus**, which means "making judgment," <note>Asmodeus is more commonly associated with lust in other traditions, but here the author emphasizes his role in the execution of punishment</note> and under his command are said to be the avengers of crimes.

The fifth is **Satan**, under whose command are the conjuring demons. It is written of him in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note> that he deceives the entire world, performing great signs and making fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of men, and thus he seduces them.

The sixth is called **Meriris**, that is, a furious and boiling spirit, to whom those spirits are subject who produce storms in the air and infect the spirits of men with plague and corrupted air.

The seventh is called **Apollyon**, or **Abaddon** in Hebrew, which means "exterminating and devastating." Under his governance are the demons called the **Furies**, who are the sowers of evils, discords, wars, devastations, and so forth.

The eighth is **Astaroth**, which means "scout," called in Greek **Diabolus**, <note>meaning "Slanderer" or "Accuser"</note> that is, the criminalizer and accuser, who in the *Apocalypse* is called the accuser of the brothers, accusing them day and night in the sight of our God.

The last is **Mammon**, which is interpreted as "greed." He has under him the lurking demons and the tempters, and these are present to every human being.

Therefore, by these types of **Evil Spirits** <term>Cacodæmonum: from the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'daimon' (spirit)</term>, since they are the "powers of the air," the human spirit or "air" is afflicted in various ways; for they do not know how to actually reach his ether and intellectual spirit, as they were expelled from heaven. The Devil is said to act in the spirit alone, or generally so, and that from the beginning, as the producer and author of sin, which he produced in Adam by his lies, through which the human race has been contaminated even to this day. For (as the wise man says) *God created man for an incorrupt condition, and made him in the image of his own very nature, but by the envy of the Devil, death came into the world (Wisdom 2:23)*, where by "death" he intends the sin that was the cause of death. Whence it was said, *The Devil is a murderer from the beginning, and stood not in the truth, because there is no truth in him (John 8)*; and elsewhere, *The Devil sins from the beginning (1 John 3)*. And the Apostle says: *Sin entered into this world through one man, and death through sin, and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned (Romans 5)*. But the author of that kind of sin was that spirit seducing with his lies.

The great indignation against God that this Prince of Malice stirred up in the Israelites—by seducing them from the true worship of God to the adoration of himself—is expressed everywhere in the Holy Scriptures. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Finally, among all the impressions of <term>Cacodemons</term> <note>From the Greek "kakos" (evil) and "daimon" (spirit); a term used in Renaissance magic and medicine for malevolent entities.</note> upon the human spirit, blasphemy is the most dangerous to both soul and body. Just as the power of the thinner airy spirits is primarily concerned with man's **phantastic spirit** <note>The faculty of the soul that produces and processes mental images or "phantasms."</note> in the perturbation of the mind alone (as has been said), so indeed some of a lower order have it as their duty to affect both the body and the spirit at the same time with plague and sickness. Thus we see that just as the highest part of the air differs from the middle, and the middle from the lowest, so we perceive that the **meteors** <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any phenomenon or disturbance in the atmosphere or the body's internal "atmosphere," such as vapors, winds, or lightning.</note> in these three regions differ from one another in both consistency and quality. Nevertheless, just as we have fiery meteors in the upper region, we also have them in the middle and lowest regions, which communicate by natural reason with earth and water. Therefore, the higher a "meteor" is produced in the air, the less commerce it is observed to have with earth and water, and the more it shares with air and fire; and all these things are governed by the **spirit of the place**.

It is no wonder, then, if some fiery spirits act only upon the human spirit, inciting fury, *lycanthropy* <note>A delusion where one believes themselves to be a wolf.</note>, anger, and heat within it. Others disturb the spirit and, through the spirit, the humors and body simultaneously. Likewise, others are observed to leave the airy spirit untouched and immune to febrile heat, but reign over and afflict the humors in the members of the body alone. For these are undoubtedly all angelic ministers <note>The author views "demons" as "fallen" angelic ministers who still carry out God's judgments.</note> through whom God afflicts the spirits and bodies of sinners, just as the Fountain of Truth testifies that He acts beneficially toward men through good angels. Whence it is written: *He wounds and heals, He strikes, and His hands shall make whole.* <note>Job 5:18; original Latin: "Ipse vulnerat & medetur, percutit, & manus eius sanabunt"</note> And elsewhere it says: *That God speaks with rebuke through pain upon the bed, and makes all his bones waste away.* <note>Job 33:19-21</note> Yet this is certain: although this office is attributed to God, His striking angel nevertheless performs it. Even Satan himself confessed this, saying: *"Put forth your hand upon him,"* etc.; and nonetheless, Satan himself afflicted Job with a most grievous ulcer from the crown of his head to the sole of his foot. <note>Job 1-2</note> Thus, God is called the ordainer who induces this or that disease, yet He uses vindictive ministers to bring His decree into action.

It is therefore within the Divine will to afflict man with "airy" diseases, in which manner Job was also vexed, as if by a hypochondriacal wind with that diabolical plague. Whence he was forced to say: *You have lifted me up into the wind or blast, you set me upon it and cause me to waste away in substance.* <note>Job 30:22; original Latin: "Eleuasti me in ventum seu flatum, ei imponis me & efficis vt defluam substantia"</note> This is as if he had been afflicted either by a windy *tympanites* or extended on all sides by flatulence, which also frequently happens in fevers where diseases are complicated. And **Albohali** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat (c. 770–c. 835), a Persian-Arab astrologer and student of Mashallah.</note> boldly states that windy and melancholic diseases are caused by evil demons.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of how spiritual forces influence human health. Having previously categorized diseases by the four elements, Fludd now provides scriptural evidence to support the claim that "airy spirits"—specifically fallen or malevolent angels—are the primary agents behind physical and mental ailments.</meta>

254          **Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.**

The royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> seems to assert that these aerial diseases arise from wicked spirits with these words: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels.* <note>Psalm 78:49. The OCR text cites verse 74, but the text reflects verse 49.</note> And elsewhere in the Holy Scripture we read that by the prayer of Elisha, the multitude of those besieging him was struck with **darkened vision** <note>original: *Scotomia*. A medical term for dizziness accompanied by the darkening of sight.</note> (2 Kings 6). It is also recorded that this same thing happened by angelic power to the Sodomites before the door of Lot's house. Mention is also made of the torment of the bowels along with gnawing colic pain, where it is found written: *You shall be sick with a disease of the intestines, until your intestines fall out because of the sickness.* <note>2 Chronicles 21:15, referring to the punishment of King Jehoram.</note> Does the Holy Scripture not intend to speak of these kinds of flatulent spirits where it is said: *The Spirit of God winnowing, and justice pursuing the unjust* (Wisdom 11:21), and elsewhere, *The power of the spirit and the spirit of virtue shall stand against them, and like a storm and a whirlwind it shall scatter them* (Wisdom 5:24). For of such a kind is the spirit of **windy epilepsy**, of **vertigo** and **darkened vision**, and of the **suffocation of the womb** <note>A historical medical term for hysteria, then believed to be caused by the womb moving or "suffocating" within the body.</note>; these spirits are accustomed to disturb and toss the patients in the manner of a Macrocosmic whirlwind.

But to come to the effects of the burning spirits—namely plagues, fevers, furies, and madness, and other things of this kind—these are undoubtedly produced by malignant spirits of both an aerial and fiery condition. Hence Job says: *The arrows of the Lord are heavy within me, the indignation of which drinks up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord wage war against me, etc.* <note>Job 6:4.</note> Here, by "terrors," he understands the evil angels who induce terrors, according to that which was cited from the Psalm: *He sent into them his anger and indignation, evil angels* (Psalm 78). And elsewhere: *You shall not be afraid for the terror by night, nor for the arrow that flies by day, nor for the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor for the destruction—or the demon—that wastes at noonday, etc.* (Psalm 91). And elsewhere it is said: *Jehovah shall strike you with a hot and burning consumption, and with a parching fever, and with dryness, and with blasting, etc.* (Deuteronomy 28:22). Where Jehovah speaks, it is understood to be Jehovah ordaining, and the angelic ministers executing. For thus, when God afflicted the Israelites with a plague, David saw the angel striking between heaven and earth; similarly it is said: *Jehovah shall strike you with madness and blindness, etc.* Even **frenzy** <note>original: *Phrenitis*.</note> and **lycanthropy** <note>A delusion in which a person believes they have turned into a wolf.</note> arise from a hidden cause of this kind, namely from the stirring up of a malignant Demon, as is clear from that possessed man living in the tombs, moved by a tumultuous rage, who was agitated by a Legion (Mark 5).

The Holy Scriptures make ample mention of the afflictions of paralytics, epileptics, lunatics, the flows of the female belly, as well as **gonorrhea**; similarly of the leprosy of Miriam, Naaman, Gehazi, and that on the forehead of King Uzziah; of the gout of Asa, of hemorrhoids, of the **King’s Evil** <note>original: *morbo regio*. Historically refers to scrofula, a skin disease believed to be cured by the touch of a monarch.</note>, ulcers, scabies, the itch, and many other things of this kind expressed in the Holy Scripture. In the designated place of the following volume, God willing, we shall speak of these more copiously (see regarding these: 2 Kings 2; 2 Chronicles 26; 2 Chronicles 16; 1 Samuel 5).

We conclude, therefore, since in this "member" <note>An editorial division of the text.</note> you have the ministers of God described—both the benevolent who do good, and the malevolent who afflict with malicious disease—acting upon the world and its creatures, as well as upon Man, who is the end and perfection of all creatures. For this reason, among the Cabbalists, Man himself has for his appropriated symbol the last of the holy letters, namely **Tau**. If these ministers are good, God uses them in clemency, goodness, and kindness toward the world and man; but if they are evil, he uses them conversely in His severity, wrath, and vengeance as a scourge, both of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm.

Indeed, it must also be understood in this place that even His good angels sometimes execute the vengeance of God and His people upon men and the world; in which respect they are nonetheless held to be "evil angels" by those who suffer their scourge. Hence Jehovah said: *Behold, I send my angel before you... for he will not bear your rebellion, for my name is in him, etc.* <note>Exodus 23:21.</note> But regarding these matters, we shall speak more copiously in the following volume where we shall treat the causes of health and disease.

The influx of the first <term>Sephirot</term><note>The Sephirot are the ten attributes or emanations in Jewish Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note>, namely those that descend from the luminous gate of <term>Keter</term><note>original: "Cheter"</note> or the Crown, which is presided over by the name **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew: "I Am," representing the highest divine essence</note>—said to represent God the Father—glide and flow downward into the first order of Angels, the **Seraphim**. From there, they are led further down by that great Angel **Metattron** into the <term>First Mover</term><note>In ancient astronomy, the *Primum Mobile* is the outermost sphere that moves all others.</note>, attributing to it the force and vigor by which it turns the celestial orbs from east to west in the space of a single day. For this reason, Metattron is established as the presiding officer of the First Mover, from which he liberally rains down essence and the faculty of motion upon the lower things. For, according to the testimony of the Kabbalists, *Ehieh* bestows the gift of being, whence it is Metattron's office to flow these virtues into all creatures. This is the reason why he is regarded as the **Soul of the World**. Furthermore, in this action, the property of God implies clemency and kindness toward the world. The outpourings of the second Sephirot—either the second "enumeration" or the luminous gate called <term>Chokmah</term><note>original: "Hochma"</note> or Wisdom (presided over by the divine name **Jah** or **Jehovah**) —fall into the order of the **Cherubim**. They are then entrusted by that order to the guardianship of the Archangel **Jophiel** (or **Raziel**, as others prefer), so that through him they may be introduced into the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the Fixed Stars</note>. From there, they are poured out into lower things, both celestial and elementary. By their virtue, the fixed stars—both within the Zodiac and outside its zone—are observed to act upon the lower world, producing various likenesses of life, and especially of animals. This is why the **Zodiac** is named from the Greek word *Zoon*, which signifies "animal." Hence it is that **Cecco d'Ascoli** <note>original: "Cichus Esculus," a 13th-century astronomer and poet</note>, in his book on the spheres, asserted not ineptly that every animal in the land and sea symbolizes and agrees in nature with some sign of the Zodiac. And **Moses the Arab** <note>The Jewish philosopher Maimonides</note> says that every animate thing has a star in heaven flowing into it to protect and preserve its essence.

But truly, since every heaven or sphere (and consequently all the stars within it) has its own great angel to move and govern it, and to conduct the influences sent to it by God through the intellectual heaven; and also since many **Principal Leaders** are subject to each of these royal Archangels, who have many legions of spirits of lower condition under their jurisdiction, we therefore say that each of these spirits <note>original: "dæmonum," used here in the classical sense of a guiding spirit or intermediary, not necessarily evil.</note> has his own peculiar office both in the heavens and in the elements. **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy and alchemy</note> seems to confirm this in part in *Pimander*, book 3, with these words: *The Gods were seen in the ideas of the stars with their signs; the stars were numbered according to the Gods who inhabited them*, where by "Gods" he seems to mean these spirits. The influx of the third Sephirot, which is <term>Binah</term> or Prudence <note>Also translated as "Understanding"</note> (over which the name of God **Elohim** presides), passes through the order of the **Thrones** and is received by the Archangel **Zaphkiel** (or **Jophiel**, as others prefer), who conducts it into the sphere of **Saturn**. From this, it gains its peculiar virtue and property, distinct from the other planets. Thus, this planet rains down Saturnine influences, or Saturnine spirits and species, upon the earth—especially at that time when it holds dominion in the heavens. For then its effects appear more evidently in the elements, which for the most part are sorrowful and hardly favorable to the world or the human spirit; hence, it is called by astrologers the **Greater Malefic** <note>original: "infortunium maius"</note>.

The influxes of the fourth enumeration or luminous gate, namely that called <term>Chesed</term> or Clemency, presided over by the name of God **El**, descend into the order of the **Dominations**. Through them, they are carried downward by the Archangel **Zadkiel** into the sphere of **Jupiter**, mercifully tempering its nature. Thus it happens that the down-flowings sent from it are benevolent and gracious to both the air and the human spirit, as they are said to nourish and foster natural powers. Hence, it is called by astrologers the **Greater Benefic** <note>original: "Fortunium maius"</note>.

The influences of the fifth luminous gate or enumeration, called <term>Geburah</term> (that is, Punishment), presided over by the name of God **Elohim Gibor**, penetrate through the order of the **Powers**. Without the Archangel **Camael** (or **Samael**), they are conducted into the sphere of **Mars**, where they animate the fiery spirits of Mars with a burning and inclement severity. Therefore, this planet is not without reason called by astrologers the **Lesser Malefic** <note>original: "infortunium minus"</note>. For just as the influences of Saturn are accustomed to act harshly upon the world’s elements and its creatures by way of extreme cold and dryness, so indeed do the Martial spirits, bearing arms under the leadership of Samael, affect the fiery air of the world with burning, lightning-flashes, comets, and many other troubles, and they infest the human spirit with heat, fever, plague, and inflammations.

The sixth luminous gate, called <term>Tiphereth</term> (that is, Grace or Beauty), overseen by the name of God **Eloah**, flows through the order of the **Virtues**. The Archangel **Michael** is, by his office, the receiver of its influxes, and he translates them into the sphere of the **Sun**. From its golden world, gracious, splendid, and life-giving virtues are rained down into the lower parts; these are called **Solar spirits**, which never act maliciously unless they are corrupted by the spirits of wicked planets.

The seventh, called <term>Netzach</term><note>original: "Netzeth"</note> or Triumph, before which is placed the name of God **Jehovah Sabaoth**, sends its benevolent inspirations into the order of the **Principalities**. From there, they are conducted downward through the Archangel **Haniel** into the sphere of **Venus**. Thus it happens that the Venerean spirits emit favorable breaths into these lower regions; for this reason, Venus is called by astrologers the **Lesser Benefic** <note>original: "Fortunium minus"</note>, seeing as she, after Jupiter...

### CHAPTER VII.

#### On the Angels of the **Sephiroth**, and first concerning that great and imperial Angel of Light called **Metattron**, and then afterwards concerning that great Angel of Darkness, opposed to him in nature and disposition.

From the twofold arrangement of divine properties poured out from the **Sephirotic** parts <note>The ten attributes or "Sephiroth" of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, through which God's essence flows into the universe.</note>, two orders of Angels arise, opposite in nature and condition. One of these is occupied with beneficence, while the other is occupied with malice toward the human race—which is the very purpose of creation. 

And upon this foundation are those philosophers established who placed two principal powers in the world: namely, **strife** and **friendship** <note>original: "litem & amicitiam." This refers to the theory of the Pre-Socratic philosopher Empedocles, who argued that the universe is governed by the forces of attraction (Love/Friendship) and repulsion (Strife).</note>, of which the latter reconciles things, while the former scatters them. Hence it happened that, just as it was the role of **Apollo**, according to the intention of the Poets, to compose and unite things with the bonds of concord, so indeed it was the property of **Dionysus** to destroy composed things through the antipathy of discord and to dissipate what was united. <note>The author uses these Greek gods as symbols for the two sides of divine action: Apollo represents the ordering, harmonious light, while Dionysus represents the breaking down or "dissolving" force.</note> 

And yet, both Apollo and Dionysus represented nothing but a single divine essence, emitting the operation of its act in two forms and according to its will—namely, either in clemency and piety...

The **Crown** <note>original: "corona," referring to Kether, the highest Sephirah on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life</note>, that primary emanation by whose power all things were brought from nothing into being and action in the blink of an eye, is itself called **Wisdom** <note>original: "sapientia"</note>. From this Wisdom, a second outflowing then emerged through the **gate of light** <note>A metaphor for the process of divine manifestation</note>, coming directly from the secret heart of the Almighty. The wise man seems to confirm this elsewhere: *Wisdom is a pure emanation or flow of the clarity of Almighty God, the brightness and whiteness of eternal light. Wisdom of Solomon 7.* It is for this reason that this God-like Angel—this emanation or flow of divine majesty—is taken to be the **Spiritual Christ**, as mentioned before. He is the one in whom the angels dwell as their King, and he encompasses the nature of both angels and God. In him, all other things find their limit. 

This is why the Kabbalists say that the angel **Metatron** is the **Prince of Faces**, because he is the mediator who introduces souls before the face of God. This is the office of the spiritual Christ himself, who is true Wisdom, proceeding first from the mouth of the Father like a son. The Prophet seems to understand this Angel when he says: *And his name shall be called the Angel of Great Counsel, Isaiah 9:6.* <note>The author cites Isaiah 6, but the quote "Angel of Great Counsel" is from the Septuagint version of Isaiah 9:6.</note> In this respect, this angel is seen as representing Christ in many places in Holy Scripture. 

More secretive theologians believe this is the angel under whose guardianship God placed Moses and the Israelites to lead them through the desert, and in whom the name of **Jehovah** resided. They say he holds dominion over the world in the same way that the **Mind**, which is the intellect, is said to rule over the human spirit. Concerning his power—namely, his dilated and universal authority—a man deep in occult **Theosophy** <note>A term for divine wisdom or mystical philosophy</note> breaks out into these words: 

*First among all is that great spirit who destines the immense and widely extended water, which is called heaven, and preserves it in its essence, and wonderfully grants motion to all growing and living things.*

This is why he is considered the **World Soul** <note>original: "anima mundi"</note> by the Platonists and other wise men. The Kabbalists understood this as the **green line** <note>In Kabbalah, the "linea viridis" often refers to a boundary or ray of light that encompasses the universe</note> which is said to encircle the entire spirit of the world. Consequently, some believe this Angel, Metatron, is the final **Midah** <note>A Hebrew term for an "attribute" or "measure"</note> or property of the Archetypal world, which others call **Kether Elyon** <note>original: "Cheter Elion," the Supreme Crown</note>. From this, "Metatron" carries the meaning "Gift of God," for the life and form of the world was the greatest of God's gifts, including all other gifts within it. 

Therefore, all those skilled in mystical philosophy seem to fall into this opinion, agreeing with the words of **Ecclesiasticus**: that just as Metatron (or this World Soul) was the first thing created among all creatures, so he is said to contain within himself the perfection of all creatures, which receive their forms from him as if from a universal fountain. This is why **Rabbi Moses** <note>Likely referring to Maimonides (Moses ben Maimon)</note> says this Angel Metatron is the prefect of the universe, or the **primary active intellect**, from whom all forms flow, and consequently by whom all individual virtues in the world—especially human ones—are governed. **Rabbi Bereshit** <note>Referring to the author of or a commentary on the Midrash Bereshit Rabbah</note> called all these virtues "angels," while others called them "forms." 

This same point seems to be suggested by those who want the mystery of the Angels (which was created along with natural things) to be contained under the common name of **Michael**, as a name for the whole angelic species, by which we are taught that all angels are of the same kind. We say, therefore, that whether the angel is called **Metatron** or **Michael**, he is nothing other than the white and pure emanation or power of God, which we previously called Wisdom. This emanation is clothed in the world-spirit as if in a garment, illuminated by its presence. The Kabbalists consider this to be the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> wrapped in the world-spirit since the beginning of the world, just as the Messiah himself was surrounded by flesh in the middle age of the world. 

Therefore, Metatron is called an "Angel" insofar as there is an "otherness"—that is, he consists of the created world-spirit as an outer part, and the uncreated divine spirit (the pure clarity of God or the emanation of clarity) as his internal part. This internal spirit is present everywhere in the world, filling, permeating, and producing all things, as it is the **Word of God** creating all. For this reason, secretive theologians consider him the Spiritual Christ or Messiah, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, as said before. This is what the wise man in Ecclesiasticus meant when he said Wisdom was created before all things—that is, mixed with the world-spirit in the manner of a creature. In this state, expanded everywhere, he fixed the heavens with their regions and the earth, gave them life, and brought them into being. This occurred during the first three days of creation, according to the opinion of Moses, which is why we have it written by the Royal Psalmist: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made (and elsewhere, by his wisdom), and all their power by the spirit of his mouth.*

When the third day was completed, **Metatron** (whom the Platonists called the World Soul for the reasons stated) contracted his rays, which had been scattered everywhere, into a single polished mass of the world—namely, into the **Sun**. This was done through the divine outflow of **Ensoph** <note>The Ein Sof, or Infinite Godhead</note> or infinity, operating from the gate of **Tiphereth** <note>original: "Triphereth," the Sephirah of Beauty and Harmony, often associated with the Sun</note>. This matches the words of the Royal Psalmist: *He set his tabernacle in the sun.* 

Just as Metatron's quality changed slightly, so too was the name **Michael** given to him, as reported before, as if one were to say, "Who is he who is like God?" This argues that it is God himself putting on a garment of light, who animates the sun, and for this reason is called the father of life and multiplication. Hence, God is also said by **David** to be clothed in light as if with a garment. In this respect, he is sometimes called an Angel, and sometimes **Jehovah**. We observe that his property was to animate the universal world-spirit, and to arrange the regions of the heavens and the elements according to the design of the **Archetype** <note>The "Archetype" refers to the divine blueprint or the mind of God in which all things exist before they are created.</note>, disposing them in harmonious peace. Thus, after three days had passed, he chose a denser tabernacle <note>The "tabernacle" here refers to the Sun, which the author views as the physical dwelling of this great spirit.</note>, so that he might more easily look upon the creatures of the elements—namely animals, plants, and minerals—and rain down upon them the gifts of quickening, germination, and generation. Similarly, the structural frameworks of the entire world which **Metatron** created in the beginning, **Michael** intends to preserve until the very end, while at the same time he looks toward those things created after the fourth day. Therefore, we see that both **Metatron** and **Michael** belong to one noble lineage, as they both proceed from the mouth of the Most High, and they agree in their office and duty: namely, in the quickening of the world and the distribution and preservation of souls or forms.

Furthermore, just as it is the office of the angel **Metatron** to introduce souls before the face of God (as the hidden theologians maintain), for which reason he is called the **Prince of Faces**, so also it is the duty of **Michael** to offer souls in heaven, as the Archangel <note>The "Archangel" here likely refers to Archangelus de Burgonovo, a 16th-century commentator on Kabbalistic texts.</note> holds in his *Commentary on Kabbalistic Dogmas*. For, as he says: *Michael is the high priest, sacrificing the immaculate souls of men to the blessed God in the upper world.* And elsewhere it is said: *Michael performs a perpetual priesthood in heaven as the great priest of God.* For just as the high priest on earth offers the souls of animals to God, so Michael, the spiritual Priest, offers rational souls to Him in heaven. By the same reasoning, **Metatron** is said to have been the leader of Moses, through whose mediation it is handed down that Moses obtained the grace of speaking with God face to face, as mentioned above: *Mouth to mouth,* says Jehovah to Aaron and Miriam, *I speak to him.*

Finally, just as it was the duty of the great angel **Metatron** to drive back the darkness, to strike down the horrendous shadows, and to hurl everything impure from heaven into the earthly abyss, so too is **Michael**, that great angel, said to fight for the souls of all against the **ancient serpent**, who continually seeks to devour them. In that battle, the Dragon having been cast out of heaven, Michael prevailed, and he reigns and shines gloriously in heaven; he always holds the dragon, or the prince of darkness, under his will and command. Thus we read in Daniel that Michael is always an aid to the people of God. The words are as follows: *Michael, the great Prince who stands for the children of the people, that is, for the elect. Daniel 12.*

Guided by these and other points, the Philosophers skilled in divine mysteries teach that the angel Michael is the very same as **Metatron**, and that Michael (whom the Sephiroth-scholars make the guardian of **Tiphereth** <note><term>Tiphereth</term>: The sixth Sephirah on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing Beauty, Harmony, and the Sun. For it is he who gives life not only to celestial and terrestrial creatures, but also preserves and defends their lives against the Prince of Darkness.

Moreover, we have all of this confirmed by the **Book of Revelation**, namely that this Angel is that spiritual **Christ** and the **Messiah** of the entire world, or the Word of God, which according to John is the light of the world, from which all things were made and without which nothing was made, as in it is life, etc. (John 1). For first, we read that he proclaimed to John while he was caught up in the spirit, crying out with a loud voice as if through a trumpet: *I am Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End; one who was like the son of man, whose eyes were like a flame of fire, and his feet like the purest molten brass glowing in a furnace; he wore a golden girdle, and in his right hand he held seven stars, and his face shone like the sun; his voice was like the murmur of many waters, etc. (Revelation 1).*

By these words, that thrice-great angel Michael seems to be most clearly and plainly described. According to Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, polymath, and influential writer on magic and angelology.</note> and others best versed in true magic, Michael is the prefect and leader of the **celestial Sun**, who placed his seat and Tabernacle in the sun. This is also declared by his appearance, which is most similar to the sun: for just as the face of a man claims its place in his upper part, while his feet rest upon the earth, so indeed the face of this Angel is likened to the sun in heaven, and his feet to the air glowing and flashing in a fiery furnace, thereby signifying the solar rays which strike the earth and the elemental region everywhere. 

And just as we observe that the sun is the lord and, as it were, the emperor of the whole sky, giving life and light not only to its own spirit but also to all its stars—which the more excellent Philosophers say have received their luminous power and their very act of existing and essence from it, not unlike how an earthly Emperor is accustomed to grant dignity and the power of acting to the kings, princes, or magistrates subject to him—so indeed we see here that this imperial angel, bearing a solar figure in his countenance, holds **seven stars** in his right hand. By this, John seems to signify that the seven stars and the Angels presiding over them are under his power. For as the material Sun is accustomed to impart its light and power to the other stars, so Michael, who is the spiritual or internal Sun in heaven, is accustomed to attribute light-giving force and vigor to the other seven angels, as he is superior to them in office and rank. 

For Dionysius, Basil, Origen, and others testify that angels of a superior order receive light more abundantly than inferior ones; they also admit that inferior angels receive their light and power from the superior ones by way of influence. Therefore, it is clear that this Angel is the most powerful of all in heaven. In this way indeed, Satan or the dragon—against whom we read that *Michael* acted manfully and with triumph in war—is the devastator of lives, the exterminator, the open enemy of salvation, the foe of generation, and the constant accuser and slanderer of souls before God. Many names have been imposed upon this head and leader of malignant spirits by the Sacred Scriptures, encompassing great hidden mysteries concerning his condition. In the first place, he was called *Lucifer* <note>The name "Lucifer" literally means "Light-bearer" (from the Latin *lux* and *ferre*).</note>; for he was made such in his origin by the Creator—namely, clearer and more splendid than the other angels, as Gregory <note>Likely referring to Pope Gregory the Great (c. 540–604 AD), a major source for medieval angelology.</note> seems to assert. The Prophet describes this in open words: *How you have fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, who rose in the morning! In this way, the first sin was committed in heaven. However, GOD had created Lucifer without sin, with clear and pure air; sin, on the other hand, was "dark air." For Lucifer and his company consisted of elements of air that were impure and mixed with the clear and pure elements of air that covered, subdued, and restrained that impure air. In this history of Lucifer (which this Author undoubtedly saw inscribed in the secret and mystical book of nature and observed in the new creation), he clearly denotes that Lucifer was created from both clear and dark air together. His pure air was his exterior, flashing with an admirable brightness, which so illuminated and tempered the wicked or dark air that the whole of Lucifer was originally created by God as good and devoid of sin. Truly, his malice and envy were the cause that his hidden darkness gradually overcame his luminous exterior, and thus he obscured his exterior with his darkness, suppressed it, and clouded it on all sides with dark air in a manifest manner. Because of this sin, he was banished in exile from the place of light, by the mediation of the luminous angels, into a dark place—namely, the air of this kind. 

Wherefore, as he was previously called Lucifer <note>original: "Lucifer," meaning "Light-bringer."</note> because of his brightness and was exalted in dignity above all the luminous angels, he is now called by some *Lucifugus* <note>original: "Lucifugus," meaning "Light-fleeing."</note>—that is, one who flees the light of God and of the good angels. Nevertheless, in this light of darkness, he holds dominion over all the angels of his company. Hence, he is called by the Apostle in one place the "prince of the power of the air," who works in the children of disobedience (Ephesians 2:2). And elsewhere, "Prince, power, and lord of darkness, the spirit of malice under heaven" (Ephesians 6). 

John, in the Apocalypse, called this Prince the "great red dragon, the ancient serpent," because of his poisonous nature and subtlety (Revelation 12). He is called "Devil" as if "rushing downward," and "Satan" as the "adversary" or "opponent." Elsewhere he is called *Behemoth*, as if a "ox" or "terrible beast like an ox," and elsewhere *Leviathan*, meaning an "addition" or "apposition" (Job 40). For as Gregory <note>Likely referring to Pope Gregory the Great's *Moralia in Job*.</note> holds, he is accustomed to add evil to evil, sin to sin, and grief to grief, as if sewing them together. He is also called the "slanderer," wherefore it is written in the Apocalypse, "The accuser has been cast down." Furthermore, he is named a "Lion" because of his open and manifest violence; hence Peter says, "As a roaring lion" (1 Peter 5). In the Apocalypse, he is called *Apollyon*, that is, "Destroyer" or "Waster," for he attempts not only to destroy men and other creatures but even to turn virtues into vices. 

Hence we also read what is written in the Prophet Isaiah: "Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord," etc. (Isaiah 54:16-17). With these words, the Prophet clearly teaches that the Devil was expressly created by God to lead men into error and make them sin, so that he might afterwards destroy them. For this reason, he calls him the "smith blowing the coals of fire" and "bringing forth his vessel"—namely, just as a smith is accustomed to shape and adapt iron with fire for his purpose into this or that form, so that he may more easily complete the work he set out to do, so indeed the Devil is accustomed to prepare his instruments, both to deceive the human spirit with flattering whispers and to openly harm the bodies of men and other creatures. 

It is for this reason that he sometimes stirs up winds to injure and destroy men and beasts. Hence it is written in Job: "Suddenly a great wind came from the direction of the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon his children" (Job 1:19). Sometimes he calls down fire from heaven and uses it to commit his deadly deeds; hence we read in the same chapter, "The fire of GOD fell from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep and the servants" (Job 1:16). Sometimes he afflicts the body with sores and plagues; thus it is said that Satan struck Job with a most grievous sore from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head (Job 2:7). Sometimes he stains the air with corruption and is accustomed to bring in pestilence to fulfill the pleasure of his creator. For we read in the prophecy of Habakkuk: "GOD shall come from the South... his glory covered the heavens... death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go forth before his feet" (Habakkuk 3:3-5). <note>The author uses a Latin translation where "pestis" (plague) or "Diabolus" is associated with the Hebrew *Resheph* (flame or plague).</note> Or, "the plague or wasting pestilence shall go before him at noon." 

From this, it is clear that the Devil is a minister of God, always ready at his feet. He contaminates the air with plague, and in this specific property, he is called *Meriris* <note>A name found in medieval grimoires and the works of Agrippa, associated with the "meridional" or southern demon of the noon-day heat.</note> by the Hebrew Magi, or the "burning demon of the south." Agrippa says this is that great Prince of malice who is said by the Apostle to have the power of the air of this world—that is, the sublunary air, which is dark air and very subject to changes compared to the empyrean or ethereal airs, which are far clearer and purer. Finally, he is the one who has power over all the winds of the sublunary world; hence, at God's command or permission, he stirs up thunders, lightnings, winds, clouds, rains, and tempests, both in the air and in the sea.

It is sometimes permitted to him [the Devil] to bring about, against the laws of worldly nature, disturbances in the sea, chasms <note>original: *Chasmata*; in Renaissance meteorology, these were seen as openings or "gaps" in the sky, often associated with auroras or unusual light phenomena</note>, comets, mists, floods, snow, hail, earthquakes, and all other **meteors** <term>Meteors: In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon (rain, wind, lightning), not just falling stars.</term>. Nevertheless, all the aforementioned things are the works and creatures of GOD, which cannot be stirred up in this world by the Devil unless God commits them into his hands. Thus, the Devil said to Jehovah: *Stretch out your hand a little and touch all that he possesses;* and Jehovah replied: *Behold, all that he has is in your hand, only do not stretch out your hand against him.* <note>Referencing the Book of Job 1:11–12, where Satan is given permission to test Job's faith.</note> By which saying, the fiery Angels of GOD, who are called the ministers of GOD, and those "windy" ones, were under his command for that time. Hence it was said, *the fire of GOD fell from heaven,* not the fire of the Devil; and yet this was at the command of the Devil. By these things it is clear that these harmful angels, although they are under the jurisdiction of the Devil, are nonetheless called the most powerful angels of GOD in strength, carrying out His word or will as much in the property of severity as in that of mercy. 

From this, the four corners of the earth and the world, and the four winds breathing from them, seem to be those four leaders who are said to carry the wide-spread sails of Satan—seeing as he is the great prince of the entire air. Just as those four angels, or spirits, or demons, are said to hold the reins of the winds, they are said to have command over the four regions of the worldly air: namely, the **East**, or (as the Hebrews would have it) **Samael**, has command over the Eastern Wind; **Paymon**, or as they prefer, **Azazel**, presides over the Western wind; **Egyn**, or (as they hand down) **Azael**, over the Northern; and **Amaymon**, or as they wish, **Mahazael**, over the Southern.

But truly, the goodness of almighty GOD is clearly declared in this: that just as He saw best and foreknew that sin was going to be introduced into the world before anything was introduced, and for this reason ordained the Devil from the beginning to punish it; so indeed His mercy has so far prevailed over His severity that He created and established good angels of ineffable virtue. Specifically, He established a single, most powerful Prince <note>Likely referring to the Archangel Michael, the traditional protector against the forces of darkness.</note> who is able to so overcome the Devil (who destroys GOD's creatures) by strength and power, that in battle he not only drove him out from the kingdom of heaven, but also dominates him in that sublunary world. The Devil is subjected to his [the Prince's] pleasure, who would inhibit and hinder the evil spirits of the winds in their malevolent duties, and also, according to the divine will, would correct the malignancy of those blasts and direct them by his infinite virtue toward prosperous effects. It is his role to give life to all things, to preserve all things, and to cherish them. 

And this we have gathered most clearly from the Apocalypse: *And I saw four angels (says the Revelator) standing on the four corners of the earth, that they should not blow upon the earth, nor upon the sea, nor upon any tree; and I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living GOD, and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: do not hurt the earth or the sea, nor the trees, until we have marked the servants of our God on their foreheads.* (Apocalypse 7). By which he seems to hint that that great and good Angel ascending from the east—whose task it was to preserve from the injury of the said malignant spirits those whom GOD had chosen, along with his angels—had power and command over those destroying spirits; for at his command, they immediately offered obedience. Now, how these spirits appointed over the evil winds hold the reins of the winds, and how they are subjected to the command of the four great Angels of God, we have delineated in the following ocular description.

...in no other way than the internal man is said to be made in the image of God, and thus has superintendence over all other things; and just as the Sun is given the chief place in heaven among all the planets as the highest and first in dignity, so the Eastern angel—being dedicated to the sun, and for this reason to be preferred above the others in dignity and place—is said to preside as **Michael**, who belongs to the side of mercy. The Archangel **Raphael** rules the region opposite to him and its spirit, namely the prefect of that West Wind <note>original: *Favonius*; the gentle western breeze in classical mythology</note>, just as **Gabriel** rules the Northern region and **Uriel** the Southern. Moreover, we have this same thing confirmed among the Hebrew Teachers: for Rabbi Tedacus Levi, in the book *On the Ten Numerations* <note>original: *De 10. Numerationib.*; referring to the ten Sefirot of the Kabbalah</note>, after explaining the four winds—the Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western—finally proceeds thus: *from those four winds he created four Angels who were set as prefects over them by day and by night. Michael, however, who is of the side of mercy and compassions, is appointed as the steward, that is, the prefect over the Eastern wind; and even until the middle of the day and until the night, Raphael rules the Western wind, who is likewise of the side of mercy. Then Gabriel, by the power of judgment and severity, is prefect with the Northern wind over half the night and two measures of the world; Noriel* <note>A variation of Uriel often found in Kabbalistic texts</note> *presides over the South:* Thus he says. But each of these also has under him an Angel of the nature of the Prince of the Air, each of whom has several species under him, which the *Book of Secrets* contains. This also seems to be confirmed by what is read in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: *Porta Lucis*; likely the *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla</note>: *From the earth,* it says, *even unto the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of forms; some of them pure, others capable of grace and compassions; and there are below many false, harmful, and tempting images, all dwelling and flying in the air—some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, some for death, and consequently some for safety and health, and some for disease and infirmity. And all of that is in the lower habitation in which we are,* as Joseph Castaliensis asserts. From this it is clear that good Angels are mixed with the foul and evil ones, so that the actions of the wicked demons (who hold God and men in ineffable hatred) may be tempered, repelled, and mitigated. And Bartholomew seems to support this assertion of ours, speaking thus: *The entire effort of the demons or wicked spirits is to do evil, and to disturb and infest men with malice; and for that reason they very often disturb the elements, stir up tempests in the air and water, and corrupt the fruits of the earth, as is explained in the Apocalypse; and they would induce far greater evils upon the inhabitants of the earth, unless the good Angels blunted the edge of their violence.* Hence it is clear that they can do nothing except by divine permission, as the good Angels are their bridles; but once permission is given, the good Angels themselves not only cease from their protection, but are even accustomed to contribute to the punishment of creatures, as we read everywhere in the sacred scriptures. Regarding the protection of the good Angels against the insults of the evil Angels, the royal Psalmist speaks thus: *Do not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that invades in the darkness, nor the encounter of the midday demon; the scourge shall not come near your tent, for he shall give his Angels charge over you in all your ways, Psalm 91.* By this speech, he clearly seems to intimate that God ordained to defend good men from the insults of wicked demons through angels of a nature contrary to theirs. But this is elegantly demonstrated through the protection of the Archangel Raphael in the book of Tobit, who, by repelling the insults of the demon Asmodeus, preserved Tobias himself immune from his rage.

We conclude, therefore, that it is most certain that just as Lucifer, now called Satan, after his fall and exile from heaven was made the universal Prince of this air, according to the saying of Saint Paul, his chief effect is from the South, which is the place from which rot is emitted, and plagues, and wasting, and where thunders are very often sent forth. Whence he is also called by the Hebrews (as was declared before) *Meririm*; that is, the demon burning and raging at midday. Or, as Habakkuk and the royal Prophet <note>King David</note> say in the places cited before, the pestilence or the demon wasting at noon or in the South. Thus, similarly, as this Prince of the Air divides his aerial kingdom into four quarters—namely East, West, South, and North—and assigns a prefect to each part by divine command, whose duty it is to make the winds blow perversely; so indeed, such was the mercy toward the things created in the sublunary heaven, and especially toward man, that in the place of that Prince of great wrath and malice in the air or this world where we live, God placed a Prince still greater and full of graces and mercy, who also has three other angels joined to him as companions and similar in property and goodness, who have force and power over those spirits acting as Satan’s lieutenants, who have power over the winds. Hence, as *Meririm* with his spirit is accustomed to rage in the south, so Michael, the great Prince who has superintendence, claims for himself the East, the hinge of the world <note>original: *Metirem*; likely a typo or variant for a term related to the world's measurements or cardinal points</note>, in which he manages the actions of Samael, or as others say, of the East, as has been said more often. For these are the words of Cornelius Agrippa: *Book 3, On Occult Philosophy, Chapter 24: Among the evil spirits, four most powerful kings preside over the others according to the four parts of the world, whose names are Uriens or Oriens, King of the East; Amaymon, King of the South; Paymon, King of the West; and Egyn, King of the North. The doctors of the Hebrews perhaps more rightly call them Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael, under whom many other princes and presidents dominate, as well as innumerable demons of private offices.* Thus he says. And yet in his Scale of the number four <note>referring to a table of correspondences for the number 4</note> he says: *There are 4 Angels presiding over the hinges of heaven: Michael over the Eastern, Raphael over the Western, Gabriel over the Northern, and Uriel over the Southern. There are 4 Prince demons harmful in the elements: Samael, Azazel, Azael, Mahazael. There are 4 Princes of demons over the 4 corners of the earth: Oriens, Paymon, Egyn, Amaymon.* By which it is clear that this author is not consistent with himself, since he here makes a difference between the four princes harmful in the elements, and those over the four corners of the world, who have the care of the winds...
